title: Shariah Computational Financial Engineering I: Reconstructing Retail FX and CFD Market Access – A Structural Incompatibility Analysis and First-Principles Alternative Architecture

detail.title: Shariah Computational Financial Engineering I: Reconstructing Retail FX and CFD Market Access – A Structural Incompatibility Analysis and First-Principles Alternative Architecture

detail.abstract: Retail contracts for difference (CFDs) and leveraged foreign exchange (FX) trading constitute one of the fastest-growing segments of global retail market access, with daily notional turnover exceeding several trillion United States dollars across major brokerages. Despite the size of the observant-Muslim retail population, no rigorous mathematical treatment of the compatibility between the standard CFD/FX architecture and Islamic contract law currently exists in the peer-reviewed literature. Drawing on primary-source observations from a Capital Markets and Trading Analyst residency at Bacera Co Pty Ltd, this paper formalises the CFD payoff mechanism, the Tom-Next overnight financing structure, and the leverage-margin dynamics as a coupled stochastic system driven by a Bates (1996) jump-diffusion with stochastic volatility. Within this formal model we document five structural incompatibilities or concerns between the standard retail CFD and the selected AAOIFI/OIC constraint framework: an interest-rate-linked financing mechanism (ribā concern), a synthetic contingent payoff without ownership or delivery (gharar concern), a counterparty-reciprocity structure under B-book execution (maysir concern), and non-fit with the classical nominate contract categories, including absence of qabd ., and a reciprocal-deferred-contingent obligation structure (bay’ al-k¯ali’ bi’l-k¯ali’ concern). We further show that the “swap-free Islamic account” variant marketed by conventional brokers addresses at most the first of these concerns and only in part. We then construct, subject to the same constraint framework, three candidate alternative market-access architectures: (i) a wa’d-based FX exposure vehicle, whose scholarly permissibility depends on whether the double-wa’d structure is admitted under the recognised authorities (this paper takes the AAOIFI restrictive reading and records the divergence); (ii) a commodity-mur¯abah .a financing overlay, whose organised form is impermissible under OIC Resolution 179; and (iii) a shar¯ıkat al ’in¯an pooled-equity structure that is formally consistent with the operational design constraints adopted in this paper, subject in every case to review by a qualified Shariah supervisory board. For each we derive the payoff dynamics and holding cost under the same underlying process. A simulation based quantitative comparison, under illustrative Bates parameterisations consistent with published FX and equity implied-volatility studies, quantifies the fee-structure differential, tail-risk properties, and margin-call trigger distributions of each architecture against a conventional leveraged CFD baseline. Because the shar¯ıkat architecture cannot be leveraged within the joint-ownership construction adopted, the comparison is properly understood as a quantification of the economic cost of the leverage cap imposed by that construction: the compliant architecture forgoes proportional leveraged upside and leveraged downside relative to a CFD of matched client capital, while removing the structural concerns identified. The paper does not issue fiqh rulings; it formalises the mathematical structure and documents its consistency, or otherwise, with the adopted constraint framework. Ultimate compliance certification remains the province of qualified Shariah supervisory boards. An open-source Python implementation is released with the paper, together with a full empirical calibration pipeline outlined as future work.

title: AI Policy In College Admissions: A Survey Of The Institutional Landscape And Its Economic Stakes

detail.title: AI Policy In College Admissions: A Survey Of The Institutional Landscape And Its Economic Stakes

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors do not have any personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced their study.
declarations.funderStatement: All authors have conducted research on their own without any funding.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has entered college admissions from two directions that are governed almost entirely separately. Institutions increasingly use AI to score essays, forecast yield, and optimize financial aid; applicants increasingly use it to write the essays those systems read. This paper surveys both, together with the economic substrate they share and the legal environment they now operate in. We review the economics of enrollment management, tuition price discrimination, and the human-capital-versus-signaling debate that describes what admission has long been asked to certify; the documented institutional deployment of AI across undergraduate, graduate, medical, and law admissions; the post-SFFA legal landscape and the 2025 federal retreat from disparateimpact enforcement, set against a fragmented state, accreditor, and international response; and the concentrated vendor market that supplies most institutional admissions AI. As an original empirical contribution, we present a hand-compiled dataset of 75 U.S. and UK institutions' published policies on applicant use of generative AI in admissions essays, coded into five tiers. Two-thirds of the sample permits AI for assistance and editing while forbidding generated text, and program-specific prohibitions concentrate sharply in art, design, and creative-writing admissions, where the submitted work is itself the evaluated artifact. A third finding concerns the evidence itself: of the 18 entries whose policy summary names an enforcement mechanism, all 18 come from a third-party aggregator, and no institution in the sample states an enforcement mechanism in its own published words. We report the dataset's limits directly: 35 of 75 entries rest on paraphrase rather than verified quotation, and 24 derive from an aggregator rather than the institution's own site. Read together, the applicant-facing and institution-facing sides of admissions AI are proceeding on separate tracks with separate rules. We argue that this disarticulation reflects a political and legal choice rather than a technical inevitability, and that narrowing it is the central unresolved question at the intersection of AI and college admissions.

title: No Treaty, No Country: The Creation of States by Agreement and the Case for Private Initiative

detail.title: No Treaty, No Country: The Creation of States by Agreement and the Case for Private Initiative

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Julien Starr is the founding director of the Startup States Society (Geneva).
declarations.funderStatement: 100.00% Self-funded

detail.abstract:
Can a treaty bring a country into being, and may a private actor lawfully set such a process in motion? This monograph examines the creation of states by international agreement from the Napoleonic settlements and the Congress of Vienna to the Republic of Cyprus in 1960, and sets out what a contemporary project would require.

It defends three findings. First, existing states, alone or acting together, have by international agreement constituted new polities, and on occasion new states, out of territory under their authority: Vatican City, the Free City of Cracow, Eastern Rumelia, Libya, and the Republic of Cyprus among them. Second, no identified case shows a state granting its own territory, by constitutive instrument, at the initiative of a private actor; private power has come close, most of all in the Congo Free State, but in none of these cases did a state grant territory it held. Third, no rule of international law treats the private origin of a proposal as a ground of invalidity for the state act that follows it, while recognition of any resulting state remains a separate political act.

The evidence is arranged on a ladder of constitutive power (conjured, codified, transformed, restored, recognised), with independence, operation, and durability assessed separately. The practical proposal, a design built from these findings rather than proved by them, rests on parent state permission and on the separation of dominium from imperium: a consenting state keeps ownership of uninhabited, undisputed land as landlord, while a new state receives governmental authority by treaty, after referendums, with no cession of title and no secession.

The monograph draws on treaties, United Nations resolutions, and judgments of international courts quoted from primary texts, and includes illustrative instrument suites, a model template, and a table of authorities. It is a work of independent research, not legal advice or a legal opinion.

detail.abstract: From the 1910s to the late 1950s, local, state, and federal retirement systems actively participated in public finance as investors in public debt. They did so, this essay argues, under a regime of 'fiscal mutualism,' where pension trustees balanced governments' needs for low-cost finance against pensioners' needs for high investment returns. This regime was supported from the institution of public employee retirement systems in the 1910s and 1920s until the early 1960s by an overlapping system of state investment restrictions, actuarial preferences, and trustee conservatism. Sustained low municipal bond yields in the 1940s and early 1950s undercut the economic viability of this system, yet rising rates amid a state government and suburban infrastructure boom from 1954 onwards revived it until about the end of the decade. At that point, changes in trust investment philosophy, understandings about the purpose of public pensions, and the professionalization of public asset management all drove public funds away from fiscal mutualisms' trade-offs and into mortgages, corporate bonds and corporate stocks.

title: A Longitudinal Perspective of Diversity in the Legal Profession
affiliations: Southern Methodist University - Dedman School of Law and University of Florida

detail.title: A Longitudinal Perspective of Diversity in the Legal Profession

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

publicationDetails.detailsText: SMU Dedman School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper No. 753
publicationDetails.journalName: Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
This Article provides needed data to empirically evaluate diversity outcomes in the legal profession using several unique lenses. We empirically model the propensity of individuals in large U.S. Census samples to work in the legal profession given their gender, ethnicity, race, and additional control variables over five time periods (1992-95, 2001-05, 2008-12, 2013-16, and 2017-20). The most important difference between our methodology and the existing literature is that we not only quantify the diversity of the legal profession, but we then empirically benchmark its diversity against carefully chosen comparison groups. Specifically, our models compare diversity in the legal profession against (1) all full-time workers, (2) full-time college educated workers who are 35 years old or younger, and (3) full-time workers in high-status professions who are 35 years old or younger. This last comparison offers the most distinctive perspective. Minority representation in all high-status professions in the United States is low relative to minority representation in the population. Structural, social, and educational inequalities, among others, result in too few individuals from historically underrepresented groups progressing through the education pipeline to qualify to enter any high-status profession, and the legal profession is no exception. By comparing diversity in the legal profession to other high-barrier, high-status professions and accounting for other factors that may influence entering these professions, we can better isolate concerns over which the legal profession may have more control. Furthermore, examining only relatively young workers helps us understand more recent diversity outcomes.

Consistent with prior research, we provide robust evidence that diversity in the legal profession is low when we benchmark it against diversity among full-time workers or against diversity among college educated workers. However, when we benchmark diversity among young members of the legal profession against diversity among young members of other high-status professions, we find evidence of consistent underrepresentation in the legal profession only for Asians. The magnitude of Asian underrepresentation in the legal profession in these comparisons is large. We estimate that a young Asian person in our sample is less likely to be a member of the legal profession than a member of another prestigious profession by between 52% and 81%, depending on the time period and specification of the model. We also perform tests examining the intersection of gender and race/ethnicity. The most consistent finding from these analyses is that Native Hawaiian/ Pacific Islander men have been overrepresented in the legal profession when compared to other high-status professions while women from this group have been underrepresented.

Finally, we examine data from millions of college freshman across a wide array of dimensions including their race/ethnicity and "probable career occupation." Our analyses show that Asian people have been significantly underrepresented among college freshman aspiring to become lawyers. In fact, when compared to other high-status professions, Asian underrepresentation among students aspiring to careers in the legal profession is between -56% and -74%. Furthermore, while Black and Hispanic college freshman aspire to join the legal profession at higher rates when compared to other professions, U.S. Census data show that Black and Hispanic people are not overrepresented among young workers in the legal profession, indicating a lost opportunity to further diversify the legal profession with respect to these racial and ethnic groups.

title: When Night Lights Miscalibrate Income: Electricity Access and Satellite-Based Measurement of Economic Activity

detail.title: When Night Lights Miscalibrate Income: Electricity Access and Satellite-Based Measurement of Economic Activity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N. A.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N. A.
declarations.funderStatement: N. A.

detail.abstract: Nighttime lights are widely used as an external signal of economic activity. Yet luminosity is not output itself: it is activity made visible through settlement, electricity infrastructure, lighting technology, and the satellite sensor. Using a global panel for 1992-2024 and country-held-out validation, this paper tests whether electricity access is a systematic calibration dimension in the mapping from nighttime luminosity to reported GDP per capita. An NTL-based benchmark that excludes electricity exhibits a positive electricity-related residual gradient after countries are compared at similar predicted income. Adding electricity substantially attenuates that gradient and modestly improves held-out prediction, especially in the complete-data and VIIRS-era samples. In a fully held-out application, Bangladesh's reported 2024 GDP per capita is 52 percent above the benchmark without electricity but 16 percent above the electricity-augmented benchmark. The results show that GDP-lights discrepancies result from disagreements between measurement systems, and thus should not be mechanically interpreted as evidence of nationalaccounts error.

detail.title: School-based measles vaccination screening and catch-up program implementation in Zambia: costing study

keywords.keywords: Measles-rubella vaccination School-based immunization Immunization costing Cost analysis Zero-dose children Immunization financing Vaccination screening and catch-up

detail.abstract: Many children in Zambia miss measles vaccination through routine immunization, while supplementary immunization activities (SIAs) targeting children under five may not reach older under-vaccinated children. School-based vaccination screening and catch-up (SVS) is a recommended strategy to identify and vaccinate these children, but evidence on its implementation and cost in sub-Saharan Africa is limited. We estimated the cost of an SVS pilot for measles vaccination in Zambia to inform implementation and potential scale-up.,We conducted an ingredients-based costing from the Government of Zambia perspective of an SVS pilot in 20 urban schools in Lusaka and rural schools in Masaiti. Costs were estimated under three scenarios: base case (full pilot costs); post-introduction (excluding start-up and technical support); and budgeting (assuming full program integration and excluding start-up, technical support, and Ministry of Health and Education staff costs). One-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. Costs are reported in 2024 USD and Zambian kwacha (ZMW).,Among 3,351 children screened, 215 were identified as measles-rubella (MR) zero-dose and 211 were vaccinated. Total implementation cost was USD 75,886 (ZMW 2,111,157) in the base case. By input, personnel accounted for 70.6% of costs. By SVS activity, coordination and training accounted for 46.8% and 34.0% of total costs, respectively. Costs decreased by 28.3% in the post-introduction and 42.3% in the budgeting scenario. Cost per child screened ranged from USD 13.05–22.65, and per MR zero-dose child vaccinated from USD 208.29–360.70. Coordination time was the most influential parameter.,While costs per child are relatively high, SVS is a targeted strategy that can be used to reach older children who remain unreached by routine immunization programs and SIAs. Efficiency could improve through streamlined documentation, integration with school health activities, and reduced coordination and personnel requirements. Further research should assess its comparative value and cost-effectiveness against other approaches.

title: Functional Legal Personality Of Autonomous AI Agents In The Agentic Internet

detail.title: Functional Legal Personality Of Autonomous AI Agents In The Agentic Internet

detail.abstract: This article examines the conditions under which limited functional legal personality may be justified for persistent autonomous AI agents. A comparison of Russian, European Union, and United States law shows that existing legal regimes already recognize the legal significance of automated conduct while continuing to vest rights and obligations in existing natural and legal persons. Building on prior scholarship concerning electronic and functional personhood, algorithmic entities, asset partitioning, insurance, machine identity, and delegation, the article proposes a specific private-law architecture for situations in which an agentic operational lineage must preserve obligations despite changes in principals, operators, and technical implementations. The model combines a two-stage necessity and admissibility test, a machine-readable mandate, a single line of legal continuity, a segregated compensation pool, mandatory traceability, and anti-shielding rules. It also compares the proposed status with competing structures, including corporate wrappers, trust and fund arrangements, and an enhanced object-based regime. Functional legal personality is defended as a conditional mechanism for attribution, continuity, and enforceability, and should not be used where existing legal forms can perform the same functions more reliably and at lower institutional cost while providing equivalent protection to creditors.

title: Gridwater: The Embedded Water Cost of Electricity

detail.title: Gridwater: The Embedded Water Cost of Electricity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Aquadrio, which operates a commercial system for metering, attributing, and valuing the water consumed in electricity generation, as described in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded

detail.abstract: Electrification is on pace to be the great infrastructure project of the 21st century. The water consumed to generate a load of electricity is currently untracked and unattributed. This embedded water — gridwater — represents a large cost that is today invisible and unpriced, and is unattributed to the water basin in which it is consumed. This is driven today by large data center buildouts, and as more energy production and consumption moves onto electric grids, gridwater consumption will continue to increase. As such, more of the world’s water will become gridwater, and is at greater risk of getting lost in our currently inadequate tracking systems. We propose a novel metering and accounting system to track, record, and attribute gridwater to the basin in which it was consumed, and to the hour of electricity that used it. Such a system should be verifiable through recomputation to ensure validity and fidelity for the hourly record it should create. Gridwater consumption must therefore be tracked per-hour and attributed per-basin in order to correctly derive the cost of the embedded water in an hour of electricity.

publicationDetails.journalName: Swiss National Bank Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Can cash infrastructure mitigate the adverse effects of a card payment system outage? As cashless payment systems become increasingly prevalent, societies are becoming more vulnerable to technical disruptions such as card payment system outages. This paper investigates a one-day nationwide card payment system outage at a major retailer in Switzerland. To quantify the loss in card sales at the retailer's stores and the increase in cash withdrawals at ATMs, we generate granular counterfactuals by forecasting card payments and cash withdrawals at the store and ATM level. We then use residual-on-residual regressions to control for high-dimensional confounders and estimate the causal effect of outage-induced card payment losses on ATM withdrawals in an event-study framework. Our district-level results suggest that for every 100 lost card payments, there were 11 additional ATM withdrawals. In value terms, for every CHF 100 loss in card payments, ATM withdrawals increased by approximately CHF 68. We also find only limited evidence of increased card payments at competing stores during the outage or at outage-affected stores on the day after the outage. Our findings suggest that cash infrastructure can serve as a resilience buffer during card payment system outages and that consumers rely on cash as their primary fallback payment instrument.

detail.abstract: In the aftermath of natural disasters and unexpected economic shocks, agents must make risky decisions with changed resources, and after experiencing the psychological effects of the shock itself. Field data combine these two factors, concealing whether the subsequent response is primarily driven by a wealth shift, a psychological-response channel, or both. We distinguish these two channels in a controlled experiment where the origin of wealth is exogenously manipulated. We find that the largest adjustments occur when the stochastic experience is accompanied by a change in resources. Within the same-wealth counterfactual, risk preferences are stable and unresponsive to the economic shock.

title: A Comparative Study on Using Machine Learning Models for Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Knee Osteoarthritis
affiliations: Iran University of Science and Technology and Iran University of Science and Technology

detail.title: A Comparative Study on Using Machine Learning Models for Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Knee Osteoarthritis
detail.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA), a leading cause of disability worldwide, remains challenging to diagnose early using conventional radiographic methods. While machine learning (ML) has shown promise in imaging-based OA detection, the integration of non-imaging clinical, demographic, and biological data for early diagnosis remains underexplored. This study leverages the NIH Osteoarthritis Initiative dataset to develop ML models that combine serum and urine biomarkers, medication histories, and clinical/demographic features to predict OA progression. First, using clinical and demographic data alone, the MLP classifier achieved outstanding performance (F1: 0.915, AUC: 0.98), demonstrating that structured patient information carries highly discriminative signals for OA prediction. When serum and urine biomarkers were analyzed, CatBoost achieved a modest F1 of 0.62 and AUC of 0.63. Notably, feature selection using RFE and Boruta improved CatBoost's F1 score by 12% compared to baseline models using all features, highlighting the value of targeted feature engineering in small-sample clinical studies. Despite lower scores compared to imaging-centric deep learning models (e.g., CNNs with AUC >0.9), this work provides a cost-effective alternative for settings lacking advanced imaging infrastructure. Key innovations include the integration of medication frequency data (MIF dataset) with biomarkers—a novel combination not previously explored—and a custom preprocessing pipeline addressing real-world challenges like byte-encoded strings, class imbalance (471 OA vs. 129 controls), and sparse medication features. While performance is constrained by dataset biases and subtle early-stage signals, our interpretable model highlights actionable predictors such as KL grade progression, NSAID usage frequency, and creatinine-adjusted biomarkers.

title: A Combined Capacity Factor-Reliability Framework for Wind Siting: A Case Study in the United States Offshore Mid-Atlantic Region

detail.title: A Combined Capacity Factor-Reliability Framework for Wind Siting: A Case Study in the United States Offshore Mid-Atlantic Region

declarations.funderStatement: The authors declare that they have no funding for the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Wind power intermittency complicates offshore wind siting because the capacity factor alone conveys nothing about the temporal consistency of generation. This study integrates a temporal variability metric alongside the capacity factor in offshore wind site selection. Using high-resolution modelled wind data for the U.S. Mid-Atlantic, a maximum drawdown--based variability metric computed on the continuous, year resolved 2015--2019 5-minute generation series is introduced to identify sites that deliver high consistency alongside high energy yield. Applied to a filtered near-shore subregion of grid cells, the metric selects six representative sites: two matched pairs with nearly identical capacity factors but contrasting maximum drawdown, a grid cell within an actively leased New York offshore wind area, and a lower-variability counterfactual site of similar capacity factor. Each site's generation profile is evaluated in a New York State capacity expansion model aligned with Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA) targets for 2035 and 2050. At matched capacity factor, lower-variability sites consistently require less battery energy capacity in both years; within the matched pairs they also curtail less offshore wind in 2050. Under the 100% low-carbon 2050 mandate these advantages reduce offshore wind LCOE by up to $32/MWh and system-wide LCOE by up to $8.7/MWh within matched pairs, and allow a lower-capacity-factor, low-variability site to outperform a higher-capacity-factor, more variable site in system cost. In 2035, when natural gas provides inexpensive flexibility, within-pair differences shrink to about $1/MWh, showing that the economic value of variability-aware siting is regime-dependent and becomes decisive only in deeply decarbonized grids. Under the uniform cost assumptions employed, these figures indicate structural cost benefits rather than precise projections. Incorporating wind resource reliability alongside capacity factor into early-stage planning thus offers a practical, generalizable framework for reducing long-term integration costs of offshore wind.

title: From Volume to Value: A Research-Led Studio Model and the Next Phase of India's Web Development Industry

detail.title: From Volume to Value: A Research-Led Studio Model and the Next Phase of India's Web Development Industry

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests or affiliations with AETHEX.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: India's web development sector is among the world's largest and fastest growing, yet the country's small businesses remain digitally underserved in a specific and often overlooked way. The binding constraint is not the absence of websites but their underperformance as business assets. Drawing on public market and survey data, this paper diagnoses a volume and price equilibrium in the domestic market, in which commodity, template driven production maximises the number of sites produced and minimises their price, while leaving conversion, ownership and local discoverability largely unaddressed. We interpret this outcome through the economics of quality uncertainty: when buyers cannot cheaply verify quality, competition collapses onto the single visible dimension of price, and suppliers respond with templates. The paper then presents the operating model of AETHEX, a research led studio, as a candidate intervention built around conversion first design, client ownership of code and data, integrated local discoverability, and transparent fixed pricing. We set out the mechanisms by which such a model could move a segment of the market from a volume equilibrium towards a value equilibrium, and we state falsifiable hypotheses for empirical testing. The paper is conceptual. It makes no claim of proven outcomes; its contribution is a diagnosis and a testable framework.

title: Commercialising Nigeria's Earth Observation Capacity: A Sustainable Satellite-Data and Geospatial Services Model for Nasrda

detail.abstract: Investment in national space programmes is often evaluated through visible assets: satellites launched, ground infrastructure established and technical capabilities acquired. Yet the economic and developmental value of Earth observation depends ultimately on whether those assets and capabilities are converted into information products and services that solve recurring problems for governments and businesses. Nigeria has developed Earth-observation capabilities through the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA), including satellite missions, data management, remote-sensing expertise, application development and a commercial subsidiary, GeoApps Plus Limited. This article argues that sustainable commercialisation requires a transition from an asset-oriented space programme to a platform-and-services model. NASRDA need not own every satellite supplying the Nigerian market or monopolise satellite-data distribution. Instead, it can combine domestic, commercial and open data; interoperable infrastructure; value-added analytics; sector-specific products; structured public procurement; and private-sector partnerships. The article diagnoses an “Earth-observation integration deficit”: Nigeria possesses many components of the value chain, but the connections between data, research, products, procurement and recurring revenue remain insufficiently developed. It proposes a five-layer architecture covering federated data supply, an Earth-observation data and services platform, analytics and productisation, sector services, and diversified revenue. It further argues for competitive neutrality, separation of regulatory and commercial functions, coordination with the Office of the Surveyor-General of the Federation, and explicit protection of open data and private downstream innovation. The central proposition is that the long-term economic value of a national space programme lies not merely in assets placed in orbit, but in the information infrastructure, services, markets and decisions those assets make possible on Earth.

detail.abstract: Connected homes increasingly combine physical infrastructure with networks, controllers, cloud services, user accounts, automation logic, and remote administration. This makes handover more than the delivery of equipment that works on commissioning day. It also creates a continuity question: what knowledge must remain with the property when the professional who integrated the system is no longer available? Existing research addresses smart-home security and privacy across the device lifecycle, device discovery, long-term safety, and the transfer of smart homes between occupants. Building-information practice likewise provides mature approaches to asset handover through the Construction to Operations Building Information Exchange (COBie), while current guidance from CEDIA, the Association for Smart Home Professionals, emphasizes professional design documentation, project records, network diagrams, control logic, credentials, integration points, power information, and change records. The gap is therefore not an absence of documentation standards or professional guidance. It is the need for a concise residential model that brings these strands together around the integrator-to-owner or integrator-to-authorized-successor transition and treats system intelligibility as part of operational continuity. This article develops a cyber-physical handover model built around four transfers: knowledge, control, resilience, and responsibility. It also proposes a three-tier minimum handover record, distinguishes record custody from risk ownership, and uses material change as the trigger for maintaining a living record. The framework is standardsinformed, adapting established documentation and information-management foundations rather than proposing a documentation system from scratch. The central argument is that technical completion and informational completion are different. A connected home is not fully handed over merely because it works; enough protected, usable knowledge must remain for a homeowner or other authorized successor to understand, operate, maintain, secure, troubleshoot, recover, and modify the system over time.

title: The Agent Payment Stack: How AI Agents Are Rewriting Stablecoin Payments

detail.title: The Agent Payment Stack: How AI Agents Are Rewriting Stablecoin Payments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit organisation. It was conducted independently.

detail.abstract: AI agents are becoming buyers. They purchase compute, data, search, media, and execution services without a human at the point of sale, and the card and wire rails they would have to use were designed around exactly that human. That mismatch is the central problem. Stablecoins fit machine payments better: they settle continuously, settle in small amounts, and can carry rules inside the transfer. This paper maps stablecoin payments into a five-layer Agent Payment Stack and argues that the missing piece is a cross-cutting AI control plane that makes risk, compliance, routing, and settlement decisions inside the payment flow instead of beside it, with an audit trail at each step. It grounds the argument in the public x402 record and separates what is already live from what is still proposed. Approach. The method is a structured synthesis: it maps the stack, reconciles the published x402 settlement census through December 2025 with primary regulatory and protocol documents, and assesses each control-plane function as live, partial, or proposed. Market estimates are labelled as estimates. Across 143.8 million end-2025 settlements worth about $42.8 million, the census shows a sub-dollar metering economy whose revenue and settlement are both concentrated; independent 2026 reporting indicates that the average ticket and settlement volume have since fallen further. The implication is that the near-term work is making agent intent legible and settlement multi-rail. The result is a plain-language reference for payment providers, card networks, and AI platforms, and a short list of the questions the data cannot yet answer. Key takeaway. The technology works and the demand has not arrived yet. x402 settles a high volume of sub-dollar payments, its average ticket keeps falling, and its 2026 settlement volume dropped sharply. The missing piece is not another rail-it is the decision layer that makes agents trustworthy to pay.

title: Gender Differences in Time Perception and Its Relation with Academic Performance: Non-Linear Dynamics in the Formation of Cognitive Systems

detail.title: Gender Differences in Time Perception and Its Relation with Academic Performance: Non-Linear Dynamics in the Formation of Cognitive Systems

detail.abstract: Introduction: Non-linear dynamics is probably much more common in the epigenetic dynamics of living beings than hitherto recognized. Here we report a case of global bifurcation triggered by gender that affects higher cognitive functions in humans. Method: We report a cross-cultural study showing deviations in time perception, as assessed by estimating the duration of brief sounds, according to their durations and to the gender of the perceiver. Results: Duration of sounds lasting less than 10 s were on average overestimated, whereas those lasting longer were underestimated; estimates of sounds shorter than 1 s were extremely inaccurate. Females consistently gave longer estimates than males. Accuracy in time estimation was correlated to academic performance in disciplines requiring mathematical or scientific skills in male, but not in female students. This difference in correlation however had nothing to do with overall skills in mathematics. Both sexes scored similarly in scientific and technical disciplines, but females had higher grades than males in languages and lower ones in physical education. Conclusion: Our results confirm existing evidence for gender differences in cognitive processing, hinting to the existence of different "mathematical intelligences" with different non-linear relationships between natural or biological mathematical intuition and time perception.

title: Measuring a Chokepoint Closure From Space: Radar Ship Counts and Gas Flaring During the 2026 Strait of Hormuz Closures

detail.title: Measuring a Chokepoint Closure From Space: Radar Ship Counts and Gas Flaring During the 2026 Strait of Hormuz Closures

detail.abstract: The Strait of Hormuz closed twice in 2026, and AIS ship tracking and official export statistics described the disruption late or incompletely. We measure the closures with two open satellite sources. Counting ships in 407 Sentinel-1 radar images of five locations between July 2025 and September 2026, and allowing for a brightness difference between Sentinel-1A and the newer 1C and 1D satellites, we find that the expected number of ships per image in the Hormuz transit corridor was 80% lower than before the war in the first closure and 81% lower in the second (Poisson; 95% confidence intervals 74-86% and 70-88%). Outside the strait, ship numbers off Fujairah rose by 46% in the second closure. Using VIIRS 375 m active fire data over 751 nights, we find that mean detected flare power at Iraq's southern fields was 84% lower in the first closure (86% on a second satellite), when exports from Basra collapsed, while flaring at the northern fields, which export by pipeline to Ceyhan, did not fall. The corridor count does not distinguish the two closures (difference −4%, 95% interval −50% to +85%), but southern flare power was about four times as high in the second. In August 2026, while officials and commercial trackers reported a recovery in Iraq's exports, PortWatch's AIS-based estimates of loadings at the Basra terminal and of tanker cargo through the strait came to about 13% and a twentieth of the loadings reported at Basra. Code and derived data are released with this paper.

title: 100GW by 2047: A Feasibility Check on India's Nuclear Power Assumption

detail.abstract: India's target of 100 gigawatts of nuclear power by 2047 is one of the most ambitious energy infrastructure commitments in the world, and one of the least scrutinised. This paper conducts a structured feasibility assessment across four dimensions: technoeconomic, legal, socioeconomic, and environmental, arguing that the programme faces binding constraints that its primary enabling instrument, the SHANTI Act 2025, does not adequately resolve. The analysis identifies three principal constraints. First, achieving the target requires commissioning approximately fifteen reactors per year at peak, against India's historical best of two or three, using a technology, Small Modular Reactors, that has never been deployed at commercial scale anywhere in the world. Second, the SHANTI Act's liability caps, as low as ₹100 crore per SMR incident, constitute a structural subsidy to private operators that undermines both the Polluter Pays principle and the public trust on which the programme's social licence depends. Third, failure to achieve the target locks in coal dependency through the 2040s, renders Net Zero 2070 functionally unachievable, and forecloses one of the most credible large-scale pathways for India's hard-to-abate industrial sectors. The paper concludes that 100 GW is worth pursuing. But the SHANTI Act, as currently designed, may be insufficient to the task of pursuing it.

title: Cost, Effort, and Effectiveness: Analyses of Increasingly Intensive Preventive Interventions of Automated Texting, Online Peer Support Groups, and Paraprofessional Health Coaching from a Hybrid Type-1 Effectiveness-Implementation Randomized Controlled Trial with Youth At-Risk for HIV

detail.title: Cost, Effort, and Effectiveness: Analyses of Increasingly Intensive Preventive Interventions of Automated Texting, Online Peer Support Groups, and Paraprofessional Health Coaching from a Hybrid Type-1 Effectiveness-Implementation Randomized Controlled Trial with Youth At-Risk for HIV

detail.abstract:
Background: Four intervention strategies were compared to reduce risk for HIV among sexual and gender minority youth (SGMY): 1) automated text messaging and monitoring (AMMI); 2) AMMI plus mobile-web peer support (AMMI + PS); 3) AMMI plus personalized strengths-based coaching, and 4) a bundled condition (AMMI + PS + Coach). A bundled condition previously significantly increased HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake among 895 SGMY in a factorial randomized controlled trial. Here, we examine the cost effectiveness of these interventions. 

Methods: We conducted time and motion studies (TMS) and cost-effectiveness analyses (CEA) to examine the relative benefits of each intervention. Coaching staff logged time via mobile app for 17 activities across four weeklong periods (equivalent to 11 full-time staff reporting weekly), informing low-, median-, and high-cost scenarios. Cost-effectiveness was assessed using predicted changes in PrEP use between baseline to 12-month follow-up, comparing total and marginal costs (incremental costs per 1% increase in PrEP use) across the four arms. 

Findings: Coaches’ efforts varied by implementation phase and the COVID-19 pandemic. Median annual costs for 200-youth cohorts were $18,638 (AMMI), $80,790 (AMMI + PS), $216,447 (AMMI + Coach), and $270,200 (bundled). The bundled arm showed the greatest PrEP use improvement (from 10·53% to 20·97%; 99·2% relative increase) and a favorable marginal cost-effectiveness ratio ($27,920 per 1% improvement). 

Interpretation: The bundled intervention yielded significant improvements in PrEP use with favorable marginal cost-effectiveness despite higher total costs, supporting it as a promising, cost-effective strategy. Integrating TMS with cost analysis offers a valuable approach for guiding implementation decisions.

title: The Price of Ethics: Liquidity and Safe Haven Properties of Responsible Physical Gold ETPs
affiliations: Universidad de León, Universidad de León and Universidad de León

detail.title: The Price of Ethics: Liquidity and Safe Haven Properties of Responsible Physical Gold ETPs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: We acknowledge financial assistance from the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation (PID2021-124950OB-I00)

detail.abstract: This paper examines the liquidity-resilience trade-off of Responsible Physical Gold ETPs compared to conventional physical gold investment vehicles. While gold is traditionally viewed as a uniform safe-haven asset, we identify a systematic "Price of Ethics" characterized by significantly higher bid-ask spreads for ethical vehicles. Using High-Dimensional Fixed Effects (HDFE) and Propensity Score Matching (PSM), the findings suggest that this responsibility premium is associated with differentiated resilience during systemic shocks. While conventional gold exhibits heightened sensitivity to bond market volatility (MOVE), Responsible Gold exhibits characteristics of a buffer, showing a positive net return response and a simultaneous surge in trading volume. Our analysis further reveals a maturation shift: the liquidity of Responsible Gold ETPs reflects a stable structural premium as the market moves away from transitory attention shocks, while the association with thematic ESG attention reverses, transitioning from initially widening spreads to compressing them as ethical mandates become embedded in market dynamics. Robustness checks using the Amihud ratio confirm that while Responsible Gold commands a transaction premium, it maintains market depth. Overall, our results suggest that Responsible Gold ETPs function as specialized defensive instruments, where higher transaction costs are balanced by enhanced price stability during systemic shocks.

title: Policy Shocks and Shifting Corridors: UK and European Student Immigration Reforms and the Mobility of South Asian International Students (2019-2026)

detail.abstract: Between 2019 and 2023, South Asia became the largest source region for international students entering the United Kingdom. The UK then changed direction: most taught students lost the right to bring family members in January 2024, the maintenance requirement rose in November 2025, and the Graduate Route will be shortened to 18 months from January 2027. This review examines how UK and European student immigration reforms between 2019 and 2026 have reshaped the mobility of students from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka. It combines a PRISMA 2020 screening of Scopus records (121 identified; 26 included), a policy timeline verified against primary government sources, and a descriptive analysis of Home Office visa statistics to June 2026 and Eurostat first-residence-permit data to 2025. South Asian main-applicant study visas to the UK rose from 26,580 in the year ending June 2019 to 196,820 in 2023, before falling to 130,689 in 2026. Dependant visas for South Asian nationals fell by 92% after the 2024 restriction. The response differed sharply by country: Indian visas fell by 42% from their peak, Pakistani visas peaked a year later and then almost halved, and Nepali visas continued to grow. EU first residence permits for education issued to South Asian citizens rose by 125% between 2019 and 2025, with Germany the leading destination for Indian students. The literature points to post-study work rights and commercial intermediaries as the main channels through which policy shapes choice, yet it has barely addressed the dependants restriction. The evidence is consistent with a pattern of policy pull-back and corridor diversion: when a destination withdraws the work and family pathways that made it attractive, intermediaries redirect demand towards lower-cost destinations that still offer work rights. The trends are descriptive rather than causal.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the effects of permit market on transition risk, whether shift to a low carbon economy can be facilitated without causing adverse impact on the economy, using a two sector Environmental Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium model featuring an emission intensity target, with free and auction based initial allocation, and financial frictions. The permit market has an asymmetric effect on different firms based on their compliance position that propagates from firms' balance sheets to banks' portfolio allocation decision. Different allocation methods lead to different environmental targets and financial policy. We show that transition risks are unavoidable, with a more pronounced impact in the auction. While free allocation avoids recession, the increased cost of production leads to recession in the auction method. These risks can be further mitigated through macroprudential policies, advance policy announcements, sectoral size and targets.

detail.abstract: The European biopharmaceutical industry is shifting from the integrated “blockbuster” model toward a more distributed ecosystem: large incumbents remain the industrial backbone, while small, research-intensive firms generate an increasing share of novel science. Using a panel of 225 EU pharmaceutical and biotechnology firms observed from 2003 to 2024, this chapter combines firm-level financial and patent data with country-level measures of venture finance and property-rights protection. It makes three findings. First, the rise of small firms within the European biopharmaceutical industry is a structural trend. Second, patenting is associated with higher sales for small firms, but not large incumbents. Third, these returns emerge only after several years and are stronger where growth capital is deeper and property-rights institutions more robust. As the sector relies more on SMEs to originate innovation, patent accessibility, effective protection, scale-up finance and IP enforcement become central to the competitiveness of Europe’s life-sciences.

title: Benign Overfitting in Realized Volatility Forecasting: A VAR approach

detail.title: Benign Overfitting in Realized Volatility Forecasting: A VAR approach
detail.abstract: We study whether over-parameterized models are suitable for predicting realized volatility across a cross-section of 41 assets related to the Dow Jones Industrial Average index. We propose an unconstrained vector autoregressive (VAR) model and reach and surpass the interpolation point by increasing the number of lags. We estimate the model using ridgeless regression equation by equation on rolling windows of 650 and 1000 daily observations. We show that the conditions for benign overfitting hold and that, consistently across stocks, the predicted MSE exhibits the typical double descent pattern. We assess performance using QLIKE, MSE, and realized utility metrics, finding that the benchmark heterogenous autoregressive (HAR) model outperforms the ridgeless VAR model on average when both rely solely on realized volatilities and VIX as predictors. This result changes in particular sub-samples. We show that the proposed approach is the most accurate model in low-volatility regimes and, after the onset of the coronavirus pandemic, in high-volatility regimes as well, becoming economically profitable by up to dozens of basis points. In these regimes, the ridgeless model is justied by the large statistical and economic gains that offset the additional computational costs of its estimation.

title: Always Tell Me the Odds: VADER, a Market-Implied Measure of Geopolitical Risk
affiliations: The University of Western Australia - UWA Business School, University of Western Australia - Business School, The University of Western Australia and The University of Western Australia

detail.title: Always Tell Me the Odds: VADER, a Market-Implied Measure of Geopolitical Risk

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Digital Finance CRC

detail.abstract: We propose VADER (Volatility of Abnormal Defence Equity Returns), a novel market-based geopolitical risk measure constructed from the conditional volatility of market-filtered defencesector returns. Unlike the widely used Caldara-Iacoviello news-based geopolitical risk index (GPR), which captures media attention rather than quantifiable risk, VADER provides a real-time, market-implied signal. Using daily data from 2002-2026, we demonstrate that VADER responds to major kinetic conflicts and captures geoeconomic events such as tariffs and sanctions. Correlation and tail-dependence tests confirm significant co-movement with GPR, particularly during crises, and show that VADER contains geopolitical information distinct from general market volatility. Additionally, Fama-French portfolio sorts reveal that VADER is a priced risk factor in the cross-section of U.S. stocks, earning an annualized premium of approximately 4.80% with a monotonic risk-return relationship after controlling for market volatility.

detail.abstract: Employment remains one of the most pressing economic challenges facing India. The limited capacity of the formal sector to generate sufficient jobs for a rapidly growing labour force has resulted in a large share of workers being absorbed into informal activities. The continued growth of the informal sector in terms of employment calls upon compilers to strengthen the methodology used to estimate gross value added (GVA). However, a large and dynamic informal sector is inherently more difficult to measure given the absence of Key Points • India's large informal sector, which accounts for the vast majority of employment, remains one of the most difficult components of the economy to measure accurately due to limited direct information on output, prices, and incomes. Although recent revisions to India's national accounts have introduced important methodological improvements, significant challenges remain in estimating informal-sector gross value added, particularly during periods of economic disruption when formal-sector trends may not accurately reflect informal-sector performance.

title: The Resolution of Direction: Calibrating Residual-Independence Tests in Finance

detail.title: The Resolution of Direction: Calibrating Residual-Independence Tests in Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Machine-learning tests of causal direction regress one series on another and ask whether the fitted residual is independent of the regressors, with a Gaussian-kernel statistic whose bandwidth is set from the residuals. Finance uses them to ask whether flows move prices and whether returns drive trading. On weekly speculative positions in twelve futures markets, the default test reports that flows direct prices at every horizon; with prices simulated independently of the positions, it reports the same in 42 percent of samples. We show why. When most pairs of cause values are tied, or the cause's scale contracts where the test is evaluated, the median-heuristic bandwidth locks onto first-stage estimation error, and the statistic stays bounded away from zero under independence. A pairwise diagnostic, computed without any dependence statistic, locates a design relative to this failure. We give three calibrations with stated domains: a joint block bootstrap under stationarity; a rotation of the outcome, exact under conditional invariance; and, for returns, a randomization of the sign given its magnitudes that holds the outcome and every magnitude-based first stage fixed. We prove that a rotation preserving only a same-period mean is not valid once the outcome's variance moves with the cause. Applied to flows, identified shocks, volatility and trading volume, the calibrated tests separate procedural artifacts from dependence the data carry, and register information in the sign of SPY's daily return about the next days' change in trading volume. A nine-step protocol organizes the results for model validation.

detail.abstract: When a district's mineral endowment becomes valuable, where does the labour go? Using minerals recorded beneath a district's ground, world price movements the district does not control and household survey data across 17 Sub-Saharan African countries, we find that a one-standard-deviation positive price shock increases share of employment of women working in agriculture by 1.3 percentage points relative to a baseline share of 43 percent. The effect is statistically significant under district-clustered inference and becomes marginal when limited number of independent price shifters were accounted for. The estimate for men is a null, and the difference between the two is imprecise and we do not establish a gender gap. We document that a mineral price rise shifts the sectoral allocation of women's work inside the districts where the minerals lie.

detail.abstract: Using 20 name-inferred Ethnic-Origin Groups and long-short portfolios based on reallocation disagreements between each group's funds and others, I find that mutual fund managers' origin-related informational advantage strengthens as origin-region geopolitical risk rises. The advantage is not evident unconditionally. Comparisons across regions and groups further reveal geographic specialization and a comparative advantage of origin-matched groups. The advantage arises primarily from stocks bought rather than sold relative to other funds. Trading intensity does not rise, yet disagreement becomes more concentrated with risk. Fund-level returns show no corresponding advantage. Investors instead withdraw from funds whose managers' origins match the region under stress.

detail.abstract: Can we explain asset price movements even with ex post observations of their drivers? Reinterpreting Roll's (1988) AFA Presidential Address, "R2," as a modern empirical exercise, we show that conventional macroeconomic, cash-flow, expectations, and flow variables deliver out-of-sample R2 values that are often negative and otherwise below 10% for monthly U.S. equity returns and are unavailable at the daily frequency. We use generative AI to extract newspaper-stated reasons from Wall Street Journal market summaries and filter out price and return language. These reasons explain around 30-40% of daily and monthly returns out of sample. Their content maps to interpretable themes, including corporate news, macroeconomic conditions, monetary policy, sentiment, and geopolitics.

detail.abstract: This paper studied the Fund Collection, Expenditure Management, and Financial Sustainability of Private Universities in Bangladesh using a mixed-methods approach. Among the 116 listed private universities, data were collected from 22 universities, randomly selected from different convenient areas of Bangladesh. For research purposes, in most cases, the name of the university and key persons have not been disclosed. The study found that the government of Bangladesh did not grant any public funds to private universities, even though they pay taxes to the government from their reserves and surpluses.  One of the study's important recommendations is that the government should grant a minimum amount to support primary infrastructure and academic development at private universities. In some cases, the practices of many private universities are neither transparent nor disclosed publicly. As the private university depends on tuition fees to raise funds, they revise tuition fees on average every two years. This puts significant financial pressure on students seeking higher education. Private universities should also revise their salary structures in line with the revised tuition fees. Only a few top-ranked private universities offered employee benefits such as regular increments, provident funds, gratuity, and performance bonuses. Both the university and the regulatory authority ensure regular account audits. There may be further research opportunities on the overall governance of the private universities.

detail.abstract: The abstract should be one concise paragraph that answers five questions: 1. What problem was investigated? 2. Why is ECD prediction important? 3. What method was developed? 4. What was found? 5. What is the practical significance? The abstract should introduce ECD as an important drilling variable associated with pressure management and well-control considerations (Ekechukwu and Adejumo 2024). It should explain that previous machine-learning research has demonstrated that surface drilling variables can predict ECD accurately, but conventional machinelearning systems generally produce point predictions rather than an explicit estimate of prediction uncertainty (Ekechukwu and Adejumo 2024). The proposed study should therefore introduce an uncertainty-aware deep-learning framework capable of producing both an ECD prediction and an associated uncertainty estimate. The abstract should mention the selected uncertainty method, such as:  Bayesian neural networks  Deep ensembles  Monte Carlo dropout  Heteroscedastic neural networks The final choice should depend on the actual methodology used. The abstract should conclude by explaining how uncertainty information could help distinguish highconfidence predictions from predictions requiring additional engineering attention.

detail.abstract:
Organizations frequently approach institutional business as a sales problem: identify an opportunity, submit a proposal, build a relationship, win a contract, and generate revenue. Across operating engagements conducted through Marie Management between 2024 and 2026, however, access to institutional markets depended upon a broader operating condition. Organizations needed sufficient internal capacity to identify opportunities, qualify them, respond credibly, execute contracts, manage institutional relationships, document performance, renew agreements, and absorb additional work without destabilizing existing operations.

This practitioner-based portfolio case study examines institutional market access as an operating-capacity problem rather than solely a business-development function. The work included institutional positioning, B2B and B2G contract infrastructure, project and contract management, organizational capacity planning, account ownership, delivery systems, renewal processes, utilization management, and expansion planning. Across documented portfolio evidence, active project and contract volume increased from 6 to 54, contract utilization increased from approximately 30% to 80%, 48 B2B and B2G project-based contracts renewed on three-to-five-year terms, and annual contract renewal reached 94% over three years. These results occurred alongside increases in project-management and workforce capacity required to carry institutional work.

The central finding is that initial market access and durable institutional market position are different operating conditions. Durable market access is achieved when the organization develops enough operating capacity to repeatedly convert institutional opportunity into executable, renewable, and expandable business. Contract acquisition without utilization leaves economic value unrealized. Growth without management capacity increases operating risk. Institutional business therefore depends upon the operating system behind the sale.

detail.abstract: When artificial-intelligence (AI) agents work in parallel, a single human reviewer may limit throughput. We study a firm's joint choice of team size and inspection intensity when the human checks agent outputs in sequence. In the interior inspection-cost regime, with a fixed cost per undetected error, the high-value decision depends on a comparison of revenue rates. If unverified production has a higher rate than every verifying configuration, optimal inspection eventually stops and team size grows in proportion to the square root of task value. In our calibration, removing the per-piece review overhead prevents abandonment. If a verifying configuration has a higher rate, inspection persists and team size stays bounded, even with fixed error costs. We derive a team-size threshold for the response of inspection to task value and compare joint optimisation with a policy that sets inspection by cost per task alone. In an illustrative calibration, that policy captures only about a third of attainable value in the highvalue limit. Scale is also bounded when error costs rise with task value, a mistake in any piece spoils the deliverable, inspection overlaps agent work, or the expected number of undetected errors is constrained. The results give a decision test for separable work and identify where its assumptions cease to hold.

title: Lower-limb Joint Angles and Torques During the Flight Phase Are Associated with Resulting Drop Jump Performance: A Two Network Approach​
affiliations: University of Tokyo, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Lower-limb Joint Angles and Torques During the Flight Phase Are Associated with Resulting Drop Jump Performance: A Two Network Approach​
detail.abstract: The drop jump (DJ) is commonly used to assess an athlete’s ability to rapidly produce force under temporal constraints. Although previous studies have primarily focused on stance phase biomechanical factors, it was hypothesized that flight phase kinematics may also be associated with resulting DJ performance. To examine this hypothesis, we applied a two-network approach to identify contemporaneous and temporal networks. Motion and ground reaction force data were recorded from 74 athletes during DJs, and time series of hip, knee, and ankle joint angles and torques were analyzed. A graphical lasso was first used to identify the critical time point most strongly associated with DJ performance and to estimate the contemporaneous network at that time point. Subsequently, vector autoregressive modeling was applied to estimate the temporal dependencies leading to this point. The results revealed that, at approximately 76% of the stance phase, greater knee and ankle joint torques were associated with greater jump height, whereas greater lower-limb joint extension and ankle plantarflexion, together with lower hip extensor torque, were associated with shorter ground contact time. Furthermore, these variables during the stance phase were associated with preceding kinematic and kinetic patterns; specifically, relatively greater hip and knee extension, together with greater hip extensor torque at flight onset, carried over through foot contact into the stance phase and was ultimately associated with shorter contact time. These results suggest that adopting a more upright posture at flight onset, together with early hip extensor torque generation, may contribute to better DJ performance.

detail.abstract:
Organizations often treat communication as a function of messaging, public relations, interpersonal skills, or information distribution. Across operating engagements conducted through Marie Management between 2024 and 2026, however, communication failures frequently reflected a deeper institutional problem: organizations lacked the infrastructure required to determine what information needed to move, who needed to receive it, who was responsible for communicating it, how quickly communication needed to occur, what documentation was required, when an issue required escalation, and who possessed authority to speak for the institution. 

This practitioner-based portfolio case study examines communication as operating infrastructure rather than as a promotional or interpersonal function. The work included internal communication flow, active listening and acknowledgment standards, executive and departmental communication protocols, customer and vendor communication, crisis-response architecture, public and risk communication, documentation standards, escalation systems, message approval, audit readiness, and information-retention requirements. The resulting architecture connected communication responsibilities to organizational roles, established recurring communication cadences, created documentation and acknowledgment requirements, distinguished routine information from urgent and crisis communication, and formalized the relationship between communication, operations, risk, accountability, and institutional trust. 

The operating model established differentiated standards across internal, external, crisis, operational, public-facing, and compliance communication. Internal information systems required defined channels, documented updates, message acknowledgment, meeting summaries, cross-departmental reporting, and escalation processes. External communication incorporated customer and vendor records, written confirmation of commitments, issue-resolution workflows, and relationship review. Crisis communication established a chain of command, centralized approval of official statements, emergency notification infrastructure, timestamped updates, and restrictions on unauthorized communication. Public and risk communication similarly established approval, legal review, media-response, disclosure, reputation-monitoring, and archival requirements. 

The central finding is that communication becomes institutional infrastructure when information movement is no longer dependent upon memory, personality, proximity to leadership, or informal relationships. Communication systems affect whether organizations can coordinate work, preserve institutional knowledge, manage risk, respond during disruption, maintain accountability, and provide stakeholders with information sufficient to understand institutional action. Public trust therefore depends not only on what an institution says, but also on whether the institution possesses a reliable operating system for knowing, verifying, communicating, documenting, and responding.

title: The Gold Standard for Capital Recovery in AI Infrastructure Investment What Fiber, Towers and Public Cloud Businesses Teach Us

detail.title: The Gold Standard for Capital Recovery in AI Infrastructure Investment What Fiber, Towers and Public Cloud Businesses Teach Us

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is driving an infrastructure investment cycle of exceptional scale. Whether that investment earns adequate returns will depend not only on growth in AI demand, but also on market structure, utilization, contractual commitments, counterparty credit, technological change and pricing. This article examines which historical infrastructure business models provide the most useful precedents for evaluating AI Infrastructure investment prospects.

The fiber-optic communications boom demonstrates that enormous demand growth does not guarantee capital recovery. Capacity became excessive relative to demand at prices capable of remunerating the original capital base, as numerous suppliers competed to fill largely undifferentiated networks whose construction costs were already sunk. By contrast, the U.S. tower-colocation sector has produced resilient cash flows through locally scarce assets, anchor tenants, long and escalating leases, high renewal propensity and attractive incremental economics from additional tenants. Public cloud offers a different successful model: hyperscalers aggregate diversified customer workloads, benefit from statistical multiplexing, control capacity expansion and add software-platform value above raw infrastructure.

AI Infrastructure currently exhibits elements of all three models. Long leases, contracted power capacity, prepayments and guarantees make some projects tower-like. Neoclouds and hyperscalers may achieve cloud-like workload aggregation. Yet fragmented build plans, reciprocal financial relationships, uncertain future pricing and a potentially large number of suppliers also create fiber-like risks.

The article distinguishes four forms of utilization: serving utilization, economic utilization, physical utilization and industry utilization. This framework helps identify which party bears the consequences of idle capacity at each layer of the AI ecosystem. The central investment test is not whether AI demand will grow and create substantial value. It is whether contracted and realized demand will grow quickly enough, at sufficiently high prices, for first owners to recover committed capital before contracts expire, equipment is repriced, counterparties fail or competing supply erodes renewal economics.

The Microsoft 365 Copilot artificial-intelligence tool was used as a research and writing aid in preparing this article, including for literature searches, source identification, drafting assistance and editorial review. All AI use was directed by the author, and all resulting material was also subjected to extensive human review, revision and verification. The article’s subject matter, analytical framework, judgments, conclusions and opinions are all the author’s own. The author accepts full responsibility for the final content.

detail.abstract: We give a finite simplex theorem. When the number of states equals the number of source signals and the source posterior likelihood-ratio vectors form a simplex, Blackwell dominance is characterized by a universal barycentric-coordinate condition. We also provide a three-state, two-signal counterexample to the sufficiency conjectured by Mu, Pomatto, Strack, and Tamuz for their many-state moment-generating-function conditions for large-sample Blackwell dominance. The pair satisfies strict comparisons on both parameter domains, all ordered Kullback-Leibler inequalities, bounded likelihood ratios and pairwise genericity, but dominance fails at every positive sample size. The finite theorem, the obstruction, and the continuum inequalities are verified in Lean 4.30 with Mathlib.

title: The Bullet Has No Tense: Declaratory Lag, Cost Externalization and the Manufacture of Police Brutality in Kenya

detail.abstract: Police brutality in Kenya is usually explained as indiscipline, poor training or bad apples. This article argues that it is better understood as an equilibrium manufactured by four interlocking ledgers: a command ledger, in which political speech converts fear into orders; an evidence ledger, in which the police control the facts of their own violence; a cost ledger, in which victims and the Treasury pay while officers and commanders do not; and a remedy ledger, in which courts declare rights after the fact. Reading the reasoning of Kenyan courts from Stephen Iregi Njuguna to the protest judgments of 2024 and 2025, the article identifies a recurrent defect it calls declaratory lag: judicial grammar is in the past tense, while the bullet has no tense at all. It exposes inconsistencies in the treatment of property, personal liability, mootness and torture. Drawing on oversight reports, scholarship, and press accounts, it proposes structural remedies that alter the ledgers rather than admonish officers. The argument matters because remedies aimed at individual officers leave the underlying equilibrium entirely intact and quietly rewarded. The article closes by asking whether a constitution that speaks only after the shot can ever be a constitution of restraint.

detail.abstract: Public sentiment indices for cryptocurrency are widely published and read as leading indicators. We test that reading on Bitcoin, pairing an archive-documented daily sentiment series (cryptocurrency wire and social-media items classified by a domain-specific transformer) with the log distance of the spot price from its lifetime time-weighted average price, over 752 daily observations from 2024-03-13 to 2026-06-01. We state at the outset that the first difference of this distance is the daily log return to five decimal places (correlation 0.99996), and we verify that substituting the raw return leaves every conclusion unchanged. Under wild-bootstrap inference robust to the heavy heteroskedasticity of these data, sentiment does not Granger-cause price movement (p = 0.630), while price movement does predict subsequent sentiment (p = 0.001); the lag-augmented Toda-Yamamoto test in levels agrees. The feedback is statistically clear but economically small: sentiment innovations account for 0.6% of ten-day-ahead forecast-error variance, and it yields no out-of-sample gain over an autoregressive benchmark (out-of-sample R-squared of -1.30%, Diebold-Mariano p = 0.385). A second result concerns measurement rather than prediction: two sentiment indicators published by the same platform over the same days correlate at -0.018, and the price-embedding Fear & Greed composite shows far stronger apparent feedback from prices than the text-derived series does. A composite that ingests price partly manufactures the causality it appears to detect; sentiment indices are not interchangeable, and their construction should be read before their coefficients are.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the June 2026 decision by Sudan's Ministry of Higher Education to mandate the return of all Sudanese universities operating abroad and in displacement areas to their original headquarters in Khartoum by August 1, 2026. Drawing on policy documents, institutional surveys, faculty statements, and World Bank economic data, the analysis situates this decision within Sudan's broader trajectory of centralized higher education governance and the catastrophic impact of the April 2023 war. The paper argues that the return policy prioritizes political symbolism over educational substance, imposing coercive compliance mechanisms that ignore the structural devastation of Khartoum's academic infrastructure, the displacement of the majority of faculty, and the financial impossibility of return for a significant proportion of students. Through a cost-benefit analysis informed by human capital theory and social reproduction perspectives, and examination of the policy's implications for foreign currency flows and human capital, the study demonstrates that the forced closure of external examination centers and the demand for immediate in-person operations risk producing not educational recovery but accelerated institutional decay and generational educational loss. The paper concludes with recommendations for a phased, voluntary, and adequately resourced approach to institutional return.
