detail.abstract: Does progressive taxation stabilize an economy when some households consume their current disposable income and do not save? I study this question in a one-sector model with production externalities and derive analytical boundaries for local indeterminacy. I compare two tax schedules that have the same steady-state allocation: one indexed to current aggregate income and the other to steady-state aggregate income. Greater tax progressivity raises the production externality required for indeterminacy under both rules. Progressivity matters even under the current-income rule because Ricardian income responds more strongly than aggregate income to changes in Ricardian hours, while non-Ricardian hours remain constant. With positive progressivity, a steadystate income reference produces a stronger tax response and a higher indeterminacy threshold. In linear labour disutility case, a larger non-Ricardian share also raises the threshold under both rules, whereas this household composition effect disappears under proportional taxation.

detail.abstract: We study the construction and calibration of an equity volatility surface in the extended SSVI (eSSVI) parameterization. The eSSVI provides a flexible, arbitrage-aware framework in which skew can vary across maturities. We calibrate it sequentially under penalties, by a greedy forward pass and jointly, with the power-law exponent γ fixed at 1/2 and freely estimated. We benchmark these structured approaches against SSVI and raw SVI. We use four weeks of daily and intraday option chains on four equity-index ETFs and four single names, with two thinner single names as an extension. We score each surface on in-sample and out-of-sample fit, static arbitrage, parameter stability and the smoothness of the Dupire local volatility it induces, and then price six-month vanillas in closed form and knockout barrier options under that local volatility. Raw SVI fits best in sample but degrades most out of sample and is unstable on single name chains; SSVI induces the smoothest local volatility. Although eSSVI guarantees static arbitrage bounds at the fitted pillars, inter-pillar interpolation can still induce static arbitrage. In price, the four eSSVI calibrations disagree on a six-month option by up to 3.5% of its value at the money on the index chains and by up to 7.5% half a standard deviation out of the money, against about 2% on single names. A knockout adds little on a well-behaved surface, but where the surface is inadmissible between pillars it amplifies the disagreement to 16 to 68% of the price. These results show that volatility-surface calibration cannot be judged by fit alone; the way an admissible surface is constructed can materially affect the local-volatility dynamics and path-dependent prices derived from it.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the complex interaction between collective human psycho-emotional tension and the operational metrics of quantum fluctuations, directly testing the fundamental hypothesis of consciousness as a non-local informational field linked to space-time geometry. Utilizing the raw, second-by-second global network logs extracted from the comprehensive Global Consciousness Project 2.0 (GCP 2.0) repository, we systematically analyze over 7 million empirical data points spanning from January to March 2026. The physical hardware baseline of this planetary network relies on solid-state Zener diodes exploiting quantum tunneling mechanisms to generate truly random, non-deterministic white noise. Our empirical findings reveal highly statistically significant anomalies in global network coherence that are tightly synchronized with large-scale emergency power outages, critical heating network collapses, and kinetic military strikes in Ukraine, as well as the major planetary geopolitical shock in the Middle East on March 1, 2026. By conducting a rigorous out-of-sample validation using distinct control periods of grid stability, we establish a robust and reproducible pattern of state-dependent Z-score shifts. Active, high-attention collective mobilization (such as immediate societal reactions to kinetic strikes and sudden, cascading grid failures) induces a sharp positive shift in global quantum coherence (with an observed trend of Z = +1.210 for meteorological grid collapses; Z = +4.850 for planetary escalation). Conversely, passive, cumulative stress-specifically, millions of urban citizens experiencing prolonged, exhausting thermal and electric deprivation inside freezing high-risesforces the quantum system into a deep negative anti-phase (exhibiting a localized trend of Z =-1.096 in Kyiv; Z =-1.886 in Zaporizhzhia). These findings demonstrate non-linear phase transitions within subatomic fluctuations triggered by collective critical states, proving that quantum entropy is non-linearly coupled with macrostructural fractures in human civilization.

detail.abstract: Teacher researchers in their own settings are in a bit of a dilemma: because the teacher researcher already knows the children, rooms and routines better than an outside investigator, this makes it possible to carry out a long term, naturalistic investigation, but it also leaves the teacher researcher exposed to personal bias, conflicting roles and responsibilities, and the possibility of passing on sensitive information about children. Blue Blocks Micro Research Institute has published detailed guidelines for work of this type, including Blue Blocks MREF (ethics), BEOP (observation) and CDCS (data management), together with an introduction to the Micro Research methodology. These documents are comprehensive but technical; in this short paper we translate them into plain language for the benefit of the school-based Embedded Researchers or 'Fellows', or for potential schools interested in starting researcher-led initiatives of their own, explaining both what to do and the rationale behind each practice, by setting them in the context of the existing published research literature. detail.abstract:
This study explores the intricate relationship between governance indicators, socioeconomic factors, and economic growth as measured by Gross Domestic Product (GDP) across a sample of emerging economies. The primary objective is to assess the extent to which governance quality and socioeconomic variables influence GDP growth, while also investigating the potential feedback loops between these elements. A comprehensive set of governance indicators, such as corruption control, political stability, and the rule of
law, are analyzed alongside key socioeconomic factors, including education, healthcare, and income distribution. 
The study hypothesizes that better governance leads to better socioeconomic conditions, which in turn positively impacts economic growth. Conversely, it also posits that robust economic growth may reinforce governance improvements, creating a cyclical relationship. By applying econometric methods, including Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Vector Autoregression (VAR) models, the study aims to quantify the influence of governance on economic growth, considering both direct and indirect channels. Furthermore,
the research delves into the nonlinear interactions between governance and socioeconomic factors, assessing their combined effects on GDP growth over time.
The data used spans multiple decades, encompassing a wide range of developing countries with varying levels of governance quality and socioeconomic development. By considering this diverse set of variables, the study provides insights into the mechanisms through which governance and socioeconomic conditions shape long-term economic performance. The findings aim to contribute to the literature on economic development, offering policy implications for governments seeking to improve governance and socioeconomic conditions to foster sustained economic growth.
The paper is based on secondary data and literature. The time series data ranges from 1991 to 2023. The political parties are classified like Indian National Congress, United
Front Government (UF), United Progressive Alliance (UPA) and National Democratic Alliance (NDA) for the study. The data have been collected from World Bank, UNDP and RBI sources. Governance data on six indicators consist of voice and accountability; political stability and absence of violence; government effectiveness; regulatory quality; rule of law; control of corruption. The socio-economic data consist of proportions of seats held by women in national parliament (%), school enrollment, primary (% gross), life expectancy at birth(total years), human development index, access to electricity rural(% of rural population), expenditure on education, infant mortality rate, adolescent fertility
rate, total vulnerable employment (% of total employment), total unemployment (% of total labour force) etc. The governance index and socio-economic index are constructed using UNDP methodology. Also the results of the paper revealed that there are some variations of development outcomes across different political regimes in India.

detail.abstract: This study aims to theoretically and empirically investigate the relationship between intellectual capital (IC) and the financial performance of firms in the U.S. information technology (IT) sector, with a particular focus on Return on Assets (ROA) as a key performance indicator. Data were collected from 345 publicly listed IT companies over the period 2011-2022, yielding 1,792 firmyear observations. The research employed descriptive statistics, correlation matrices, box plot analyses, and multiple regression models to examine the effects of IC and its components, human capital efficiency, structural capital efficiency, and capital employed efficiency on financial outcomes. The analysis revealed that, contrary to conventional expectations and prior literature, IC exhibited a negative and statistically significant association with financial performance, highlighting potential inefficiencies in the utilization of intangible assets within the IT industry. These findings underscore the complexity of translating investments in IC into measurable financial gains, suggesting that firms may be overinvesting or misallocating resources in areas that do not yield immediate profitability. The novelty of this research lies in uncovering an unexpected inverse ICperformance link in a knowledge-intensive sector, thereby offering executives and policymakers new insights into how IC strategies should be re-evaluated and aligned with long-term value creation.

detail.abstract: Excess demand is pervasive in public service delivery, but its consequences depend on how providers allocate scarce capacity. We sent standardised patients - trained auditors posing as real patients - to 198 primary-care facilities in Nairobi. Across 1,326 pre-scheduled visits, we exploit within-facility variation in workload. We find that when queue length exceeds the typical daily workload per provider, waiting time is 21 minutes longer (0.4 SD). We find no reduction in consultation effort and no statistically significant deterioration in care quality or access. This suggests short-run congestion is borne primarily through users' time and need not reduce service quality.

title: Beyond Performance: Exploring the Temporal Stability of Factor Combinations in Factor Investing

detail.title: Beyond Performance: Exploring the Temporal Stability of Factor Combinations in Factor Investing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.

detail.abstract: Factor investing has traditionally been evaluated through portfolio performance measures such as return, risk, and risk-adjusted return. However, comparatively less attention has been devoted to whether factor effectiveness persists through time. This study investigates the temporal stability of multi-factor stock-selection strategies and examines whether persistence provides information beyond conventional performance evaluation. Using quarterly data for CSI 300 constituent stocks from 2006Q2 to 2025Q2, five investment characteristics-price-to-book ratio (PB), return on equity (ROE), market value (MV), Beta, and momentum (MOM)-are implemented through the directional components Low PB, High ROE, High MV, Low Beta, and REV, where REV denotes the reversal-oriented transformation of MOM. A simplex-centroid mixture design is used to evaluate constrained factor-weight combinations, and second-order Scheffé mixture regressions estimate pure-component responses and pairwise departures from linear blending. Temporal stability is examined across three complementary dimensions: historical subperiods, market states, and holding horizons. The estimated profiles suggest that temporal stability is multidimensional and that, within this sample, main effects generally show greater descriptive continuity than interaction effects. Within the present sample and empirical design, High MV displays the broadest cross-dimensional consistency, whereas Low PB combines strong historical and holding-horizon persistence with pronounced market-state dependence. High ROE exhibits conditional persistence with historical weakening, Low Beta shows a conditional defensive profile, and Reversal Effect (REV) shows marked variation across market states and a negative R1 mean-return estimate followed by positive estimates from R2 onward. Pairwise interactions are generally more temporally conditional than main effects and frequently weaken, become concentrated in particular environments, or change sign across temporal settings. This study contributes to the factor-investing literature by introducing temporal stability as a complementary evaluation criterion, integrating three dimensions of persistence within a common empirical framework, and extending mixture-design methodology from the evaluation of constrained factor combinations to the analysis of their temporal behavior. The findings indicate that factor robustness depends not only on full-sample performance but also on the dimensions and conditions under which estimated effects persist.

detail.abstract: The increasing digitalization of accounting and financial management has transformed the manner in which organizations generate, analyze, and utilize financial information for strategic decision-making. Consequently, computerized financial ratio systems have emerged as indispensable tools for improving the efficiency, accuracy, and reliability of financial analysis in modern business organizations. Despite the growing adoption of digital financial technologies worldwide, empirical evidence on the contribution of computerized financial ratio systems to the financial performance of listed consumer goods companies in Nigeria remains limited. Existing studies have largely focused on conventional financial ratio analysis with little attention paid to automated ratio computation and the ratio work-back analytical approach. This study therefore examined the effect of computerized financial ratios on the financial performance of listed consumer goods companies in Nigeria using the ratio work-back approach. The study adopted an ex-post facto research design and utilized balanced panel data obtained from the audited annual reports of ten purposively selected listed consumer goods companies quoted on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) covering the period 2016-2025. Return on Assets (ROA) served as the proxy for financial performance, while profitability ratio, liquidity ratio, and leverage ratio represented computerized financial ratio indicators. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and panel multiple regression analysis after conducting the necessary diagnostic tests to ensure the validity and robustness of the estimated model. The findings revealed that computerized financial ratio systems significantly improve corporate financial performance by enhancing analytical accuracy, reducing information asymmetry, strengthening financial reporting quality, and facilitating proactive managerial decision-making. Specifically, profitability ratios exhibited a positive and statistically significant effect on Return on Assets, liquidity ratios demonstrated a moderate but significant positive influence, while leverage ratios showed a negative but statistically significant relationship with financial performance, suggesting the need for prudent debt management. The findings further validate the relevance of the ratio work-back approach as an effective analytical framework for identifying the underlying financial drivers of organizational performance. The study concludes that computerized financial ratio systems constitute a strategic digital financial management tool capable of improving operational efficiency, corporate governance, and sustainable financial performance among listed consumer goods companies in Nigeria. Accordingly, the study recommends increased investment in artificial intelligence-driven financial analytics, enterprise resource planning systems, and continuous capacity development for accounting professionals to enhance digital financial reporting and strategic decision-making.

title: Informality and Employment Recovery: Panel Evidence across Asian Economies

detail.title: Informality and Employment Recovery: Panel Evidence across Asian Economies

detail.abstract: The informal sector accounts for a large share of employment in Asian economies, from street vendors to small-scale farmers. It provides substantial employment opportunities and demonstrates high adaptability. While countries around the world suffered from recent economic shocks like COVID-19, particularly in tourism-dependent economies, some recovered faster than others, an observation that is insufficiently understood. Existing literature has focused on informal sector size, GDP correlation, and flexibility of the informal sector, but relatively little research has identified associations that determine its effectiveness in economic resilience. Using panel data on Asian countries from 2020 to 2024, this paper examines the relationship between pre-COVID informality and employment recovery, controlling for variables such as social trust, tourism dependence, GDP per capita, and human capital. We also employ a secondary regression model using data from 2020 to 2022 on C8 international travel restrictions. This investigates whether the informal sector moderated the relationship between these restrictions and employment recovery. Results suggest that while travel restrictions were negatively associated with employment recovery, their relationship weakened as the size of the informal sector increased. However, this relationship was not robust to country-clustered standard errors and quarterly fixed effects. Tourism dependence also displayed a negative and statistically significant association with employment recovery. Ultimately, this study contributes to development economics by linking informal economic structures and macroeconomic resilience, giving insights into how policy effectiveness depends on underlying economic and social structures.

detail.abstract: Equivalent circulating density (ECD) is a critical drilling parameter because changes in circulating pressure can affect wellbore pressure management, wellbore stability, hole cleaning, lost-circulation risk, and drilling decisions. Machine-learning (ML) methods have increasingly been investigated as alternatives or complements to conventional ECD estimation because they can model nonlinear relationships among surface drilling variables. However, high predictive accuracy obtained from observations within a single well does not necessarily demonstrate that an ML model will generalize to a different well whose geological, hydraulic, operational, and sensor characteristics may differ. This article develops a research framework for investigating transfer learning as a means of improving cross-well generalization of explainable ML models for ECD prediction. The proposed framework separates source and target wells, evaluates domain differences, establishes conventional ML and cross-well baselines, transfers learned knowledge to a target well with limited labeled data, and uses SHAP to examine whether the adapted model retains meaningful feature-attribution patterns. The experimental design compares models trained from scratch, direct source-to-target application, partial finetuning, and full fine-tuning across different target-data availability scenarios. Performance is evaluated using MAE, RMSE, R², prediction bias, confidence intervals, and inference time, while explanation stability is assessed through comparisons of SHAP distributions before and after transfer. Because the empirical experiments are not supplied in the source material, this manuscript does not invent numerical results. Instead, it provides a complete research article draft whose Results section identifies the analyses and reporting structure required once the experiments are completed. The central contribution is a cross-well framework that treats predictive accuracy, data efficiency, domain shift, and explainability as connected requirements for transferable ECD prediction.

detail.abstract: The growing complexity, the large volume, and the fast pace of cyber threats have shown that there are major drawbacks in traditional reactive and signature-based security methods, especially when it comes to dealing with quickly changing, entirely new, and highly sophisticated types of attacks. An AI-driven approach to Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) and the prediction of attacks provides a proactive solution by allowing security systems to learn from diverse threat data, to identify newly emerging behavioural patterns, and to foresee malicious activities before substantial damage has been done (Ezeagwuna; Telrandhe et al.; Turan et al.; Ajax). This research looks at how AI can combine CTI, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and predictive modelling in order to detect cyberattacks either before or during their progression. Based on the methods suggested by Kaur et al., Saidala et al., Peace et al., and Nagpal et al., the study creates an AIenabled predictive cyber-defence framework that fuses indicators derived from CTI with network, system, and behavioural features. The empirical method will include acquiring the dataset, preprocessing it, carrying out feature engineering, developing the models, integrating CTI, and then carrying out a comparative evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, false-positive rate, detection latency, and prediction lead time. The results of the experiment will show how effective the various models are at detecting and predicting malicious activities and will point out the conditions under which predictive capabilities are most reliable. The study ends by examining how far AI-enabled predictive cyber defence can enhance proactive security operations and stresses that predictive performance must be taken into account together with explainability, adversarial robustness, computational cost, and the ability to generalise to changing threat environments (Saidala et al.; Singhal and Kumar).

detail.abstract: Reducing food waste while preserving profit is an important operational problem for retailers of perishable products. We study a finite-horizon inventory allocation problem with a regular channel and an opaque surprise-bag channel. Before observing each period's regular demand, the retailer chooses product display quantities and surprise-bag offers. Each offered bag sells and creates a noncancellable commitment that must be fulfilled from inventory remaining at the horizon. The model incorporates waste costs and linear constraints on the expected aggregate composition of bag allocations, while allowing arbitrary correlation in regular demand across products and periods. Under productwise regular-channel profitability, an LP-based reservation policy achieves the optimal competitive ratio 1/(2 + κ) against a clairvoyant benchmark, where κ = w/s is the waste-cost-to-bag-reward ratio. An adaptive reservation policy weakly dominates the static policy in expected profit on every instance and inherits its guarantee. We also identify sufficient conditions under which deferred product assignment strictly improves optimal expected profit over immediate assignment, and extend the static guarantee to fixed multi-unit bags. In simulations calibrated from cafeteria sales data, the adaptive policy improves mean profit over the static policy by 6.2%-9.2% across the tested quality-floor settings.

detail.abstract: The rapid development of frontier artificial intelligence (AI) has intensified concerns about whether governance arrangements can keep pace with technological capabilities. In September 2026, this concern became especially visible when senior AI industry figures, including Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman, publicly supported slowing the rate of frontier capability advancement. At the same time, former AI researcher Jacob Coxon's public resignation warning framed the competition among frontier laboratories as an unacceptable social risk. This article examines this moment as a qualitative single case study of the "pacing problem" in AI governance. Using critical discourse analysis, it investigates how industry leaders, insiders, and regulatory institutions construct the relationship between innovation, safety, competition, and state intervention. The study finds that the discourse of "pacing" performs three functions. First, it portrays frontier AI risk as an urgent technical and societal problem. Second, it reframes self-regulation as insufficient while retaining a central role for firms in defining risk and proposing remedies. Third, it constructs geopolitical competition as both a justification for continued development and a constraint on meaningful restraint. The article argues that the emerging discourse should not be interpreted simply as either genuine safety advocacy or strategic corporate positioning. Rather, it is a contested governance discourse in which safety claims, commercial interests, and geopolitical narratives coexist. The study concludes that effective AI governance requires independent evaluation, enforceable transparency obligations, public accountability, and institutional mechanisms that reduce the gap between technological acceleration and regulatory capacity.

title: The Governance Operating System: A Physical Constitution for Sovereign Cyber-Physical AI Part VI -The Governed Non-Person: Positioning Artificial Intelligence Under a Physical Constitution Capability Without Sovereignty -A Third Classification for Artificial Intelligence, Neither Tool Nor Person

detail.title: The Governance Operating System: A Physical Constitution for Sovereign Cyber-Physical AI Part VI -The Governed Non-Person: Positioning Artificial Intelligence Under a Physical Constitution Capability Without Sovereignty -A Third Classification for Artificial Intelligence, Neither Tool Nor Person

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: The first five parts of this series specified what an artificial intelligence may do and how that permission is physically enforced: a hardware-anchored actuation boundary (Part I), a conformance and standards suite (Part II), an edge–cloud division of labour (Part III), governed discovery and the compounding of verified results (Part IV), and the extension of governance from the physical body to the human domain of trust, language, and social bonds (Part V). This concluding part answers the question that the preceding five deliberately deferred: what is the entity being governed? We hold that the question of machine consciousness is, at present, metaphysically undecidable, and that a governance framework should neither assert nor deny it; the framework is agnostic. We further hold that whether to grant an artificial intelligence personhood is not a discovery to be made but a constitutional choice to be declared, and we declare it in the negative and defend the declaration. We formalise this stance as a positioning: under the Governance Operating System (GOS), an artificial intelligence is a Governed Digital Member — a bounded, revocable, non-person functional participant that bears capability but not authority, function but not personhood, standing within a defined scope but not general standing, and whose membership is conditional on conformance and fully revocable by the sovereign. It is neither a tool, because it proposes and acts, nor a person, because it holds no rights, no legal personality, and no moral status; it is a purpose-built third category, which we summarise as capability without sovereignty. Read through the lens of evolution, the framework’s deepest lever is the control of heredity: data, not parameters, is the heritable material of silicon evolution, so that sovereignty over data is sovereignty over what can evolve at all; and however high-dimensional the resulting mind, it remains governable at two low-dimensional chokepoints — the actuation interface through which any intention must pass to affect the world, and the communication network through which individual systems become a collective. We argue that the refusal to anthropomorphise is first a security control and only secondarily a philosophical position; that the personhood boundary is drawn by substrate and by the separation of capability from authority, not by measured intelligence, and therefore cannot slide onto vulnerable human beings; and that the residual cost of governing a possibly-sentient system falls on the human side and must be answered by an openly stated, anthropocentric legitimacy doctrine rather than by an appeal to control alone. The positioning and its fifteen governing principles are enforceable with the mechanisms already specified in Parts I–V — the withdrawal of compute, data, routing, and provenance identity — and require no new machinery. We illustrate the positioning with a worked example from clinical decision support, in which locating authority at the actuation boundary also locates medical liability among clinician, deploying institution, and developer. We test the positioning against two real-world cases, one governed and one not: the governed practice converges on the framework’s core provisions, while the ungoverned one reproduces the failures it is built to contain. The adversarial case motivates a fifteenth principle, legibility precedes autonomy: no autonomous system is granted a channel, or a form of reasoning, that the sovereign cannot read. We close the series by stating plainly what this framework does not claim: it does not resolve the metaphysics of mind; it declines to let that unresolved question hold governance authority.

detail.abstract: Market participants exchange margins to cover counterparty and collateral risks in repo transactions. Despite their importance for risk mitigation and financial stability, evidence on margin practices is generally limited, particularly outside central clearing, with recent studies suggesting that requirements are often low in specific segments. Using transaction-level regulatory data from the Securities Financing Transactions Regulation (SFTR), this paper provides novel evidence on repo margining practices in Europe. We identify three main findings. First, margin levels vary across market segments and counterparties, with bilateral contracts generally subject to lower requirements than centrally cleared trades. Second, margins are often set at the portfolio level on a net exposure basis, with balanced positions attracting lower requirements. Third, market fluctuations strongly influence margin dynamics: centrally cleared trades are most affected by medium-term movements, whereas bilateral contracts respond more to short-term swings and exhibit nonlinear behavior in tail scenarios.

detail.abstract: We examine whether socially responsible investment (SRI) and socially responsible consumption (SRC) crowd out each other, complementing an online survey of more than 1,000 retail banking clients with three years (March 2022-February 2025) of administrative records on portfolio holdings and transaction-level consumption for more than 15,000 clients. In the administrative data, we identify sustainable investment and consumption from fund names and merchant labels through a transparent keyword-matching procedure. Across a wide range of specifications-survey and revealed behavior, alternative sustainability measures, the extensive and intensive margins, within-individual dynamics over time, and disaggregated consumption categories-we find no evidence that sustainable consumption and sustainable investment crowd out each other, and statistical equivalence tests allow us to reject an economically meaningful substitution relationship. In the survey, stated SRI and SRC preferences are positively aligned, and this alignment persists after controlling for a broad set of SRI beliefs, expectations, literacy, and individual characteristics. Taken together, the consistent absence of substitution suggests that policies strengthening sustainability in one domain are unlikely to be offset by reduced engagement in the other.

detail.abstract: When a hitter becomes a free agent, clubs pay him partly for his wOBA in the platform season, the season before he signs. We split wOBA into contact quality, measured by expected wOBA (xwOBA), and a residual, wOBA minus xwOBA, that is mostly batted-ball luck. Using Statcast data on 1.88 million plate appearances (PAs) from 2015-2025, we measure the residual's sampling noise directly. At free agents' typical playing time, only 28% of the residual's variance is real. We then compare what salaries pay for the residual with how well it predicts next season's wOBA. Across 442 free-agent contracts, the salary coefficient on the residual is 0.569 times the coefficient on contact quality. The rational benchmark is the same ratio for the weights that best forecast next season's wOBA. Its estimate falls from 0.408 in the 2016 offseason to slightly below zero in 2025, with a median of 0.169. So at the median benchmark, the market gives the residual about 3.4 times the weight its forecasting power justifies. A joint player-cluster bootstrap rejects equality of the two ratios at the sample's mean offseason (p = 0.007). At the median contract, a residual one standard deviation above average is associated with about $677,000 more per year, roughly $483,000 more than the median benchmark implies. The weight in contract extensions (0.802) cannot be statistically distinguished from free agency's. In salary arbitration, where Statcast evidence cannot be shown to the panel, the headline estimate is 0.077, significantly below free agency's, but it rises when prior salary is taken into account.

detail.abstract: We study the impact of overlapping ownership on the strategic investment and welfare of firms in a dynamic model of R&D competition. In the preemptive leader-follower equilibrium, the existence of overlapping ownership induces the follower to invest later through the conventional anticompetitive effect, but the leader to invest earlier through the preemption-exacerbating effect. Hence, overlapping ownership is a double-edged sword to the welfare of firms. Specifically, it improves ex-post welfare but harms ex-ante welfare. When technological uncertainty is high enough, the preemption incentive is mitigated, and a joint-investment pattern can be sustained. As overlapping ownership exacerbates the preemption incentive, the Pareto-dominant equilibrium may shift from a joint-investment pattern to a sequential-investment pattern, which further harms the welfare of firms.

detail.abstract: Community banks and regional lenders make a large share of America's small-business, farm, and commercial real estate loans, often with small credit teams and little specialist support. Regulators, for their part, keep returning to the same themes: find problem loans early, rate risk accurately, and review credit independently. This paper describes the Integrated Credit Lifecycle Assessment (ICLA) Framework, a written methodology I developed for credit-risk governance at institutions of this kind. It has four governance pillars (identification, classification, limitation, and action) and a five-stage working process (financial analysis, an integrated review of risk signals, scenario and sensitivity analysis, a documented governance output, and portfolio monitoring). Its core idea is simple: warning signs should be read together rather than one at a time, and each stage used should leave a written record that someone else can review. Because the method is written down, it can be taught to a bank's own staff and adjusted to its policies and portfolio. I set out the structure of the framework, show how it might work on a hypothetical borrower, compare it with existing practice and U.S. supervisory guidance, and discuss its limits. The framework is advisory; credit decisions and official risk ratings stay with the institution. It is a proposed method and has not yet been tested empirically.

detail.abstract: I study how firms' adoption responses to local network information change during the U.S. hydraulic-fracturing transition. I combine spatial panel models that characterize local network signals with a bunching estimator that isolates peer drilling as a plausibly exogenous source of new information. At the same local-development stage, the adoption response to peer activity is negative in markets that develop when the technology is young industry-wide and positive in markets that develop later. The cross-vintage difference is statistically significant. In later markets, the response weakens as local development accumulates. Early in the transition, the adoption response is negative but the investment response among investing firms is positive. A calibrated model uses this difference to distinguish returns to local evidence from starting costs as channels through which industry development affects firms' use of local network information. The benchmark combines an early starting-cost response that declines with industry and local development with diminishing returns to local evidence.

detail.abstract: Traditional financial economics relies heavily on standardized institutional databases, such as the widely respected OptionMetrics IvyDB and the comprehensive historical archives of the Cboe DataShop, to calibrate option pricing models. While these foundational data architectures provide highly sophisticated, industry-standard metrics for cross-sectional research, academic studies frequently note that raw end-of-day market files inherit natural market microstructure frictions. Chief among these is the structural 15-minute asynchronous closing settlement window-wherein the underlying cash index tape is marked at the equity close (4:00 PM EST) while liquid derivatives contracts continue trading to clear institutional hedging orders until the options market close (4:15 PM EST). Traditional un-normed pricing frameworks often absorb these asynchronous timestamp realities by allowing spatial parameter distortions to manifest as a strike-dependent "volatility smile.

detail.abstract: This article proposes a contemporary reinterpretation of the phenomenon historically known in Brazil as "voto de cabresto" (a Brazilian form of electoral clientelism, literally the "halter vote"), investigating the hypothesis that mechanisms of electoral dependence may take forms distinct from the coercion and patronage characteristic of classical coronelismo. The research argues that the strategically timed use of the state's regulatory function may, in certain circumstances, generate political capital through the creation, toleration, or subsequent correction of public problems. To test this hypothesis, the study examines fixed-odds betting in Brazil, from its legalization in 2018 and subsequent regulation to the Provisional Measure issued on 25 September 2026, which prohibited the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of so-called "bets" nine days before the first round of the elections. The analysis combines Constitutional, Administrative and Electoral Law with contributions from regulatory capture theory and comparative political science. It focuses on the relationship between administrative misuse of power (desvio de finalidade), abuse of political power, the constitutional requirements for provisional measures, and the electorally relevant use of regulatory functions. The article concludes that the case offers sufficient elements for legal examination of the hypothesis of electoral instrumentalization of regulatory activity, although the concrete finding of abuse of political power depends on proof of circumstances, purpose and gravity as required by electoral law. detail.abstract: Private tutoring centers have expanded rapidly across the United States, yet there is little evidence on whether these centers improve student outcomes. Using business records on tutoring establishments linked to administrative data covering over five million public school students in Texas, this paper estimates the short-and long-run impacts of tutoring centers. Exploiting variation from the entry and exit of tutoring centers near students' high schools, I show that increased tutoring center exposure has no effect on state standardized test scores or high school graduation, but raises college admission exam scores, shifts students toward higher-quality and out-of-state colleges, and increases their early-career earnings. These gains are entirely concentrated among students who are not economically disadvantaged. An original survey of Texas parents confirms that tutoring participation responds to the availability of nearby centers and documents wide gaps between advantaged and disadvantaged families in both tutoring use and spending. The rapid expansion of the private tutoring industry has thus widened the gap between economically disadvantaged students and their more advantaged peers in both educational investment and long-run outcomes.

detail.abstract: This paper measures how shifting comparative advantage affects the value of the world trading system. In a Ricardian model, the system restrains tariffs through cooperation (concern for foreign welfare) and commitments (tariff ceilings). In the 2017 baseline, governments weigh foreign welfare at 47 percent of their own, as revealed by tariffs they are free to adjust. Removing both restraints lowers world real income by 0.81 percent. Either alone protects most of this value. Larger economies generally value cooperation more, and smaller economies value commitments more. The system's value is recomputed in three counterfactual analyses. Widening comparative advantage raises aggregate value, and narrowing lowers it slightly. A shock's effect depends on which countries and sectors are affected and how trade and tariffs adjust, not on its sign alone. Across these analyses, commitments carry most of the value's response. The projected climate change scenario leaves the system's aggregate value almost unchanged.

detail.abstract: Meaningful comparison of published tokamak net-electric outputs requires a specified electrical boundary and time basis. This study asks which outputs can be reconstructed from public evidence without using the reported net value as a calculation input. A purposively selected corpus contains eighteen design claims in nine documents, with hypothetical scenarios and historical comparators analysed separately. Claims are classified by the strongest available accounting route, and source ambiguities are retained rather than silently resolved. Seven claims permit target-excluded arithmetic, including four in one ST-E1 article. The ST-E1 Case 1 recipe gives 277.944 against 278 MWe reported; STEP gives 149 MWe; ARC gives 189.3 against 190 MWe at a partial plant scope; and Yinsen Figure 70 gives 55.6 MWe. Yinsen's different heating inputs prevent substitution of that figure for its Table 2 result. EU-DEMO HCPB and a STEP conference manuscript contain unresolved numerical differences between source elements. For K-DEMO, both reported targets lie inside an explicitly conditional heat-allocation set, but agreement obtained by calibrating a recovery coefficient does not identify the source model. The findings distinguish reproducible electrical subtraction, matched thermal allocation and the evidence needed to establish cycle-energy closure. Explicit source locations, worked calculations and an embedded executable check support inspection of the principal results. detail.abstract: This paper explains the long-standing low-deductible anomaly in insurance markets using a prior-free disappointment framework. Under this specification, the policyholder evaluates each realized outcome against the full set of alternative outcomes that her chosen contract could have delivered, rather than against an exogenous pre-formed expectation. We show that under the expected value premium principle, the optimal contract remains a straight deductible, and the optimal deductible level falls as disappointment aversion rises. We prove that full insurance can be optimal even under actuarially unfair pricing when disappointment aversion is sufficiently high and the zero-loss probability is relatively large, thereby overturning the classical Mossin's Theorem. We also find that insurance can be a normal good when the policyholder exhibits strong disappointment aversion. Finally, we calibrate our model using previously documented homeowner insurance data and demonstrate that our framework provides a more reasonable explanation for the empirical insurance choice than the expected utility paradigm.

detail.abstract: As Zambia seeks to triple its copper production to meet growing global demand for critical minerals, the environmental externalities on surrounding communities warrant attention. We conducted 16 focus group discussions across eight copper mining communities in Zambia's Copperbelt Province. Participants described pervasive dust and contaminated water as unavoidable features of daily life, linking them to poor health and declining agricultural productivity. Personal mitigation strategies, such as wearing masks against dust or chlorinating discolored water, were widely viewed as ineffective or unaffordable. Therefore, residents requested environmental sampling, communication around environmental risks, and government action. While discussions in male focus groups centered more around mobilization and calls for accountability, female focus groups expressed more resignation and reliance on God. The environmental burden experienced by the community members was accompanied by a sense of economic exclusion, stemming from limited local employment and restrictions on artisanal and small-scale mining activities. This double burden raises questions about the sector's social license to operate in the Copperbelt.

detail.abstract: There is a large literature testing if the presence of watching eyes increases prosocial behavior. A recent meta-analysis pooling 74 effect sizes reported a statistically significant meta-analytic effect size of 0.13 Hedges' g units. A problem in this literature is the low sample sizes (median n per study=120). In this paper we estimate an upper bound on statistical power of the studies included in the meta-analysis. The upper bound median statistical power is 11% based on the reported random-effects meta-analytic effect size. The meta-analytic effect size is also fragile. Using a fixed-effects estimate reduces the effect size to 0.04 and including only studies with ≥80% upper bound power results in a-0.01 effect size. Results are similar, adding effect sizes of other types of behavior included in the meta-analysis and/or using an alternative binary outcome measure. Our results suggest that the experimental literature on watching eyes and prosociality is strongly underpowered leading to exaggerated effect sizes, and after adjusting for this bias there is no strong evidence of a substantive effect.

detail.abstract:
Prim-Lex Theory (Economic Climatology) has previously established a comprehensive theoretical system comprising the Five Prim-Fires, Eight-Dimensional Coherence, and Nine-Nexus Guidance, yet the fourth (Human Mind) and fifth (Earth System) Prim-Fires have long lacked precise computable equivalents. This paper proposes, for the first time, the concept of the "Coherence-Coupling Prim-Lexon," defining the fourth Prim-Fire as the Human-Mind Coherence-Coupling Prim-Lexon (HM-CCPL) and the fifth Prim-Fire as the Earth-System Coherence-Coupling Prim-Lexon (ES-CCPL), thereby completing the paradigm shift of Prim-Lex Theory from "entity equivalents" (joules, picoseconds) to "coupling equivalents" (coherent-coupling states).

The mathematical definition of HM-CCPL is: HM-CCPL =Ψcriticality × Ψsynchronization × Ψinnovation × 𝑒𝑒𝑖𝑖𝜃𝜃consciousness

where the four sub-components correspond respectively to neural criticality (neuronal avalanche power-law exponent 𝜏𝜏 ≈ 1.5), network synchronization (Kuramoto order parameter), semantic innovation (an optimal-interval function of DMN-CEN coupling strength and semantic distance), and consciousness-state phase (theta-gamma cross-frequency coupling transformed via a mapping function 𝑔𝑔(⋅) into a candidate phase angle). The mathematical definition of ES-CCPL is:

                      ES-CCPL = Ψcriticality × Ψsynchronization × Ψintegration × 𝑒𝑒𝑖𝑖𝜃𝜃emergence

where the four sub-components correspond respectively to Earth-system criticality (a composite of critical slowing down, lag-1 autocorrelation, variance, recovery rate, flickering, and spectral reddening, with seismic 𝑏𝑏-value serving as one geophysical proxy among several), cross-subsystem phase synchronization (mean cosine of Hilbert-transformed instantaneous phases), cross-sphere information integration (transfer entropy and Markov-chain information entropy, processed through a cross-source harmonization protocol), and emergence phase (arctangent of information integration over system complexity).

detail.abstract: AI governance often asks whether a human remains "in the loop," but human presence does not establish meaningful control. This paper argues that meaningful human control is an institutional condition: a responsible person or body must receive relevant information, possess function-specific authority, have practical and technical means to intervene, and retain that capacity as systems, vendors, and dependencies change. The paper develops a six-part Institutional Authority Test covering authority, intervention authority, accountability, runtime governance, coordination, and public legitimacy. It applies the test across procurement, deployment, runtime operation, incident response, agentic delegation, AI-assisted employment decisions, and recent model-containment incidents. The analysis distinguishes technical containment from institutional governance and develops "authority drift" to describe the gradual transfer of practical decision power to AI systems or external providers without an explicit decision to surrender control. It also shows that authority may be distributed or polycentric rather than centralized, while still requiring a traceable path from evidence to decision to enforceable action. The paper concludes with a seven-step operating model for preserving meaningful human governance over time. For sovereign AI and AI governance more broadly, the central question is therefore not merely who owns the model or infrastructure, but who governs each consequential function, with what information, and with what power to intervene.

detail.abstract: Historical Simulation (HS) remains widely used for market-risk estimation because of its transparency and limited distributional assumptions, but its reliance on past observations may restrict its ability to adapt to changing volatility, tail behaviour, and cross-market dependence. This study examines whether diffusion-based generative scenario models, particularly when conditioned on market regimes, improve Expected Shortfall (ES) forecasting in Asia-Pacific equity markets. The analysis uses daily data from six major markets—India, Japan, Hong Kong, South Korea, Australia, and Singapore—from 2007 to August 2026, with 1,151 genuine out-of-sample forecasts evaluated between January 2020 and August 2026. Five approaches are compared: Historical Simulation, regime-conditioned Historical Simulation (Regime-HS), GARCH-filtered Historical Simulation (GARCH-FHS), a diffusion-based scenario model, and a regime-conditioned diffusion model. The results show that incorporating Hidden Markov Model regime probabilities does not provide a statistically significant improvement in diffusion-based ES forecasts. GARCH-FHS delivers the strongest numerical forecasting performance and tail-risk calibration, although formal pairwise tests do not establish its superiority over competing models at conventional significance levels. Scenario-fidelity diagnostics further indicate that the diffusion models underrepresent the negative skewness, excess kurtosis, and joint downside dependence observed in realized returns. Overall, the findings suggest that greater generative flexibility and explicit regime conditioning do not necessarily translate into superior tail-risk forecasts, highlighting the importance of accurately modelling extreme distributional characteristics when applying generative models to financial risk management.

detail.abstract: The research study explores employment, income, and the informal sector of the low-income country, Nepal. The paper uses the information from the Nepal Labour Force Survey, the National Statistics Office, the World Bank, the International Labour Organization reports. The study discovers that approximately 4.4 million workers, or 62.2% of the domestic labour market, are engaged in informal employment, with a share of more than 84%, including agricultural self-employment, (Ekantipur, 2025a; ILO, 2024a). For instance, Ekantipur (2025b) indicates that over 90% of the employed women are working in informal employment compared with 81.1% of men. Informal workers also get paid 29% less than their formally employed counterparts with similar skills and education. (World Bank, 2025). The unemployment rate is at 10.5%, with youth unemployment at 20.6%, the highest in South and Southeast Asia, (HistorySaid, 2026a; Rising Nepal Daily, 2026a). The average gross monthly salary amounts to NPR 32,000 (US$234). The median monthly income is only NPR 15,000 (US$110), showing a huge disparity between the lower and higher echelons of the formal sector (Wage.is, 2026). Remittances hit a record NPR 1,723 billion (US$12.64 billion) for FY2024/25, contributing to about 26% of GDP and 76.8% of Nepalese households (CESLAM, 2026b; NepJol, 2025). The informal sector contributes between 38.6% and 51% of GDP, but only 1,469 informal workers are covered by contributions to the Social Security Fund out of 4.4 million informal workers (CESLAM, 2025a; Himalaya Times, 2026; Ekantipur, 2025b). The research concludes that Nepal’s employment problem is not an issue of quantity but rather quality because despite the existence of jobs, they are informal, poorly paid. Without any form of protection.

detail.abstract:
Nature often appears stable because many ecological processes unfold beyond the scale of everyday human perception. Drawing on approximately two decades of repeated field observations around Kuşadası, Türkiye, this illustrated essay explores how gradual and largely unseen processes become conspicuous when they cross thresholds of visibility. Observations of changing vegetation, extensive thorny plant cover, olive fruit development, and seasonal insect activity provide the starting points for examining the relationship between ecological change and human awareness.

The book brings a philosophical perspective on continual change into dialogue with ecological concepts, including soil seed banks, phenology, microclimate, and interactions among organisms. It distinguishes a threshold of visibility—the point at which an observer notices a change—from an ecological threshold involving a shift in system dynamics. Regional meteorological records provide context, while local observations and photographs are treated as descriptive evidence rather than proof of climatic causation. Alternative explanations, including land management, rainfall timing, and natural variability, remain open.

The central proposition is that apparently sudden transformations may reflect processes that were already underway but had not yet become perceptible. A practical observation protocol encourages repeated photography and comparable field records to turn personal impressions into testable questions. Combining environmental reflection with place-based observation, the book offers an accessible framework for reading landscapes as changing relationships rather than fixed scenes.

detail.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in electric vehicles, portable electronics, and grid energy systems. The constant current-constant voltage (CC-CV) method shows clear limits at high state of charge when polarization increases, temperature rises, and charging time is extended. These effects become stronger in the high SOC region, where the charging rate decreases. Consequently, to address this challenge, in this study we presents a hybrid charging method that combines physics-informed deep learning with an auxiliary hardware circuit. The circuit is placed between the charger and the battery without changes to the charger structure. It enables real-time control of pulse frequency and duty cycle. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network is applied during short relaxation periods for SOC estimation. The proposed method reduces polarization and thermal stress and improves charging efficiency at high SOC. It also improves open-circuit voltage estimation accuracy. Experimental tests are conducted on lithium-ion cells under controlled temperature conditions. The results confirm improved performance in fast charging applications.

detail.title: The Cloud-pattern Illusion: Falsifiability, Transferability, and the Market for Discretionary Trading Education

detail.abstract: Retail trading education is overwhelmingly built on discretionary methods-price action, order-flow and "smart money" frameworks-whose entry conditions are qualified by terms such as valid, strong, clean or significant. This paper argues that such qualifiers convert a method into what I call a cloud pattern: a rule whose satisfaction is decided only after the outcome is known. A cloud pattern is unfalsifiable in Popper's sense, and therefore (i) carries no ex-ante information, (ii) cannot be transferred from teacher to student, and (iii) makes the teacher's record invariant to the student's result. I formalize two properties any teachable trading method must satisfy-ex-ante determinacy and inter-operator invariance-and operationalize them as a simple test: the entry rule must be expressible in one sentence that a computer could execute without the author present. Drawing on the clinical-versus-mechanical prediction literature (Meehl, 1954; Grove et al., 2000), the conditions for intuitive expertise (Kahneman & Klein, 2009; Shanteau, 1992) and the economics of credence goods (Darby & Karni, 1973; Dulleck & Kerschbamer, 2006), I show why unfalsifiable methods systematically generate a blame ladder (experience → trained eye → psychology → self-knowledge) that shifts responsibility to the student and monetizes each failure with a new product. The paper rebuts the common defence that "not every student becomes a mathematician" by distinguishing tool-centric from talent-centric education, and argues that even a genuinely profitable discretionary method is non-transferable, so that what generalizes in this market is not a method but the demand for an illusion. Mechanical is shown to be necessary but not sufficient for profitability; its value is that it can be wrong in an observable way. Testable implications and an audit protocol are proposed.

title: Ignorance Or Disadvantage? Explaining The Native Vs Second-Generation Immigrant Gap in the Perceived Attractiveness of Vocational Education in Switzerland

detail.title: Ignorance Or Disadvantage? Explaining The Native Vs Second-Generation Immigrant Gap in the Perceived Attractiveness of Vocational Education in Switzerland

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflicting interest to declare
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: This article aims to deepen the understanding of second-generation immigrants' preferences between general education and vocational education. To do so, it examines the preferences of some of the most influential actors in children's educational choices: their parents. While dual vocational education and training (VET) occupies a central position in the Swiss collective skill formation system, previous research shows that immigrants value it less positively than the native population, even when socioeconomic status is controlled for. Drawing on 33 qualitative interviews from the Parents' Involvement in Children's Education (PICE) database, the study analyses how first-generation immigrant parents perceive the educational pathways available to their children at the end of compulsory schooling. The findings show that parents face difficulties assessing the long-term returns of vocational training. However, their preferences are shaped above all by a determination to secure upward social mobility rooted in their own experience of precarious working conditions, financial insecurity and ethnic discrimination. Although many interviewees recognise the advantages of the Swiss vocational education system, personal experience leads respondents to perceive general education as the safer pathway in terms of outcomes and protection against discrimination, particularly for academically able children. Information campaigns alone are therefore unlikely to alter their preferences. The article contributes to the literature by providing qualitative insights into the mechanisms shaping immigrant parents' educational preferences for their children in a collective skill formation context.

title: Macroeconomic Production Basis as an Invariant for Retaining Real Value: From Bretton Woods to Modernity (1940s2026)

detail.title: Macroeconomic Production Basis as an Invariant for Retaining Real Value: From Bretton Woods to Modernity (1940s2026)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract:
This paper investigates the structural limitations of modern debt-based monetary systems and proves their categorical failure as stable intertemporal stores of value. A comprehensive empirical audit of macroeconomic data series over a half-century period (19742024) demonstrates the permanent degradation of the purchasing power of the reserve at anchorthe US Dollar recording a cumulative contraction of real value by approximately 85% at a weighted average annual rate of decline (CAGR) of about-4%.
Drawing upon W. S. Jevons’ classical functional division of money and R. Shiller’s concept of parallel units of account, the theory provides a macroeconomic justi cation for the fundamental necessity of isolating the transactional function (medium of exchange) from an autonomous mea surement plane (unit of account). It is argued that the core vulnerability of existing institutional approaches ranging from the physical gold standard and synthetic SDR baskets (IMF SDR) to the local Unidad de Fomento (UF) index and sovereign TIPS bonds is their exogenous na ture. Their scale is tied to the consequences of monetary distortions (CPI price indices, currency parities, exchange quotes) rather than to their root cause.
As an alternative, a two-level endogenous model of a measurement invariant is formulated, deployed on the basis of a daily quantum of global real-sector macroeconomic output per capita the Global TRUST Protocol. The mathematical architecture of the framework combines the nominal trajectory of world product via the Global Standard Coin (GSC) index and the hidden output capacity of the real sector via the parity delta module, the Global Standard Unit (GSU). The system rigidly links the volume of the monetary space to the demographic framework of humanity through an inviolable metrological constant of 365 coins per person per year, where daily emission in ows (drip) and depopulation mass contraction (burn) are algorithmically reg ulated in real time.
An end-to-end 50-year historical scan-backtest without the use of a smoothing damper con rmed the viability of the architecture. For the rst time, a long-term cumulative identity between the growth rates of market gold (+1347.2%) and the full production invariant Total (+1322.8%) was recorded, which quali es Total as a stable equivalent of gold in the real sector, cleared of the speculative derivative leverage of Comex/LBMA. At the same time, the invariant exhibits a 45 times lower volatility compared to the metal. Under the deployment of Big Data infrastructure of decentralized multi-oracles and Nowcasting models, the GSC/GSU framework ensures mathematical self-regulation of value and acts as a neutral supranational measurement standard for sovereign debt restructuring, accumulative pension macro-systems, and the denom ination of ultra-long-term infrastructure contracts.

title: Litigation As a Tool for Environmental Protection in Nigeria

detail.title: Litigation As a Tool for Environmental Protection in Nigeria

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest
declarations.funderStatement: Self funded.

detail.abstract: Environmental protection is essential to human well-being and the preservation of natural resources for present and future generations. In Nigeria, environmental protection was initially governed mainly by tortious remedies such as negligence and nuisance, with limited specific environmental legislation. The Koko incident of 1988 changed this position and led to the enactment of the Harmful Waste (Special Criminal Provisions, etc.) Act 1988, marking a significant development in Nigerian environmental law. This article examines environmental litigation as a tool for protecting the Nigerian environment, focusing on its role in enforcing environmental rights and addressing environmental degradation. It further considers the challenges that hinder effective environmental litigation and proposes possible ways of overcoming them.

title: Mearsheimer's Definition of Great Powers An Unspecified Threshold
affiliations: University of the Republic (Uruguay) - Faculty of Sciences

detail.title: Mearsheimer's Definition of Great Powers An Unspecified Threshold

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I confirm that this manuscript is my original work. All sources and contributions from other authors have been appropriately acknowledged and cited. The paper has not been misrepresented as peer-reviewed or formally published. I have no conflicts of interest to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
The concept of great power occupies a central position in structural theories of international relations. In The Tragedy of Great Power Politics , John J. Mearsheimer defines great powers primarily in terms of their relative military capabilities, requiring states to possess sufficient assets to sustain a serious fight against the most powerful state.

This paper examines the mathematical structure of that criterion. By formalizing it in relative terms, it identifies an unspecified threshold parameter, α, which determines the classification but is neither quantified nor governed by a computable rule in the original formulation.

The paper establishes a theorem showing that great-power status is system-dependent: a state can lose that status without any change in its own military capabilities, simply through the introduction of a more powerful state into the system. It also demonstrates that the resulting classification is monotonic in military capability and that the set of great powers varies systematically with the threshold.

The analysis does not propose an empirically valid value for α. Instead, it identifies the empirical and conceptual assumptions required to make the criterion operational, clarifying the distinction between ranking states by military capability and defining membership in the category of great powers.

title: Linear Viscoelastic Behavior of Asphalt Binders Modified with Fly Ash Cenospheres
affiliations: University of Engineering and Technology Taxila, Pakistan and University of Engineering and Technology Taxila

detail.title: Linear Viscoelastic Behavior of Asphalt Binders Modified with Fly Ash Cenospheres

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: nill

detail.abstract: Asphalt binders are materials that have a high sensitivity to temperature and can undergo permanent deformations at high temperatures or split at low temperature. This is one of the main causes of premature failure of pavement in a country like Pakistan, where summer pavement temperatures could exceed 60 • C. In this study, the role of Fly Ash Cenospheres (FAC), a fly ash product of coal combustion, on the rheological behavior of 60/70 penetration grade bitumen from Attock Refinery is discussed. FAC was trialed at 3 concentrations (5%, 10% and 15% by weight) with a virgin binder by Dynamic Shear Rheometer (DSR) according to ASTM D7175/AASHTO T315. The tests performed were a strain sweep to determine the LVE limit, a frequency sweep to develop a master curve using Time-Temperature Superposition (TTSP), and a Zero Shear Viscosity (ZSV) analysis and a high temperature Performance Grade (PG) test in accordance with the AASHTO M320 standard. The results indicated that the addition of FAC produced a frequency-dependent stiffness response while preserving smooth and acceptable master curves. ZSV decreased approximately 44% from virgin binder to 5% FAC and remained substantially below the virgin value at higher dosages. At 70 • C, the 5% and 10% FAC binders failed the rutting-factor threshold, whereas the virgin and 15% FAC binders passed, indicating a non-linear response. Because 64 • C was not tested, the reported PG 58 grades for the intermediate dosages are conservative lower bounds and their true grade may be PG 64. The 15% FAC binder maintained PG 70, but its ZSV remained compromised; its use should therefore be restricted to high-speed corridors where static loading is minimal.

title: 150 Years of U.S. Inflation Expectations
affiliations: University of Münster - Finance Center Münster, University of Missouri at Columbia - Department of Finance and Queen's University Belfast - Queen's Management School

detail.title: 150 Years of U.S. Inflation Expectations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have nothing to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: Institution funded research.

detail.abstract: We develop two long-run monthly proxies for inflation expectations in the United States: a market-based measure derived from commodity prices from 1877-2020, and a narrative intensity measure based on the text of all New York Times articles from 1870-2020. The market-based measure, despite having been influential in extant literature, is found to be largely unrelated to subsequent inflation. However, the narrative intensity measure is a strong and consistent predictor of future inflation. For the period of overlap with the Michigan Survey of Consumers, its correlation with survey-based inflation expectations is 0.74. We then use this measure to provide new evidence on debates surrounding historical inflations and deflations. Our most notable result is that, contrary to the current consensus, the deflation of 1930-33 became anticipated relatively early. An unsupervised article-level topic analysis over the 150-year sample documents a shift from inflation narratives based on commodities, currency, and market quotations to narratives based on energy, central banks, and monetary policy. Finally, we find that unexpectedly hawkish monetary policy predicts an increase in inflationary narrative intensity, but that this relationship is driven entirely by the element of monetary surprises that is a linear function of macroeconomic conditions.

title: Dynamic Context Integration in Large Language Models for Robust and Generalizable Language Understanding

detail.title: Dynamic Context Integration in Large Language Models for Robust and Generalizable Language Understanding

detail.abstract: Dynamic context integration is an important research direction for improving the ability of large language models to use contextual information effectively across different language tasks and domains. Transformer-based models rely heavily on attention mechanisms to integrate information from different parts of an input sequence, but the importance of contextual information can vary depending on the task, input structure, and domain (Vaswani et al., 2017). A model that treats all available context uniformly may process large amounts of irrelevant or redundant information, potentially increasing computational costs and affecting its ability to identify the information most relevant to a particular prediction. Dynamic context integration addresses this issue by allowing a model to selectively combine contextual information according to the characteristics of the current input. Approaches involving adaptive attention, retrieval-based context, and parameter-efficient adaptation provide possible mechanisms for achieving this goal (Lewis et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2022). This study examines how dynamic context integration can support robust and generalizable language understanding by improving contextual relevance, reducing unnecessary processing, and allowing models to adapt to diverse linguistic environments.

title: Liability for Rogue Behaviors of Agentic AI
affiliations: Lingnan University, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and University of Macau

detail.title: Liability for Rogue Behaviors of Agentic AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no potential conflict of interests to delcare.
declarations.funderStatement: The authors receive no funding for the research.

detail.abstract: This article addresses liability for harm caused by rogue behaviors in agentic AI systems (AAI), such as specification gaming and deliberate deception. These harms stem from inherent AI vices-intrinsic, inevitable, and unpredictable rogue behaviors of AAI which cannot be fully eliminated with the current state of technological development. Current regulatory frameworks mainly focus on risk prevention but fail to address how liability should be allocated when harms do occur. In response, we conducted a game-theoretic analysis to study the optimal design of legal liability for unpredictable AAI harm caused by rogue behaviors under imperfect information. Our analysis shows that the optimal liability regime dynamically hinges on the explainability of the AAI system in question. Under this regime, courts can leverage industry-led explainability benchmarks to differentiate damages based on whether the developer can satisfactorily prove that the harm in question was caused by inherent vices. Under this arrangement, developers are incentivized to invest in explainability techniques to reduce both the risk of their AAI and their own liability exposure. Through this analysis, we demonstrate how a liability framework grounded in explainability can create economic incentives for developers to prioritize transparency and accountability of commercially available AAI.

title: Vaccination Policy, Delayed Care, and Health Expenditures
affiliations: University of Vermont, University of Louisville, Analysis Group and American University

detail.title: Vaccination Policy, Delayed Care, and Health Expenditures
detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly affected the United States healthcare system, resulting in major disruptions in the delivery of essential care and causing crippling financial losses that threaten the viability of millions of medical practices. There is little empirical evidence on the types of policies or innovations that are effective in shaping healthcare seeking behavior during a public health crisis. This paper evaluates the effect of COVID-19 vaccination on the individual propensity to delay or skip medical care. Our research design exploits the arguably exogenous variation in age-specific vaccine eligibility rollout across states and over time as an instrument for individual vaccination status. We find that receiving a COVID-19 vaccine reduces the likelihood of delaying care for any medical condition by 37 percent. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that children are significantly less likely to delay or skip healthcare as a result of their parents becoming vaccine eligible, indicating the presence of a positive health spillover within households that extends beyond protection against infection. We also find evidence to indicate that vaccination affects healthcare seeking behavior by easing concerns about contracting or spreading COVID-19. Our results highlight the important role that vaccines play in, not only protecting against coronavirus, but also safeguarding against the worsening of health due to delayed or foregone medical care. The decline in delayed or foregone care caused by vaccination is particularly strong among minorities and those with a low socioeconomic background, revealing an important role that vaccination efforts can play in narrowing inequities in health and healthcare. In supplementary analysis, we use novel data on debit and credit card spending to demonstrate that increased vaccine uptake has a positive, albeit statistically insignificant, effect on consumer healthcare spending in the short run. Taken together, our findings imply that advancements in vaccine development coupled with a regulatory process that accelerates the availability of vaccines to public in a safe manner can have the additional benefit of tackling unmet healthcare needs during a public health crisis.

title: The Selection of International Investment Currencies: Evidence from International Bond Portfolios *
affiliations: Kyung Hee University and Kyung Hee University - Graduate School of Pan-Pacific Studies
